definition_en: the act of making a bad condition, problem, or feeling worse or more intense
core_image: 一滴苦汁搅进清水，越搅越苦、越难下咽
scene: 医生翻看病历，发现病人昨夜喘得比前一天更厉害。The nurse noted an exacerbation of asthma after the cold snap.
sceneCN: 这里 exacerbation 是「加重、恶化」（第 1 个义项：病情突然加重）；句意：护士注意到寒潮过后病人的哮喘加重了。

derivatives.zh: 由名词去后缀 -ation 还原的动词，义为「使恶化；加剧；激怒」
动词加 -ing 构成的形容词，义为「使情况恶化的；令人恼火的」
过去分词转作的形容词，义为「被加重的；被激怒的」

senses.title: A worsening of a disease
senses.definition: a sudden increase in the severity of a disease or of its symptoms
senses.definitionCN: 疾病或其症状严重程度的突然上升
senses.example: The patient was admitted with an acute exacerbation of asthma.
senses.exampleCN: 病人因哮喘急性加重而入院。
senses.why: Latin acerbus means bitter and harsh, and exacerbare means to make a thing more bitter, so the noun first names a disease turning harsher.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 acerbus 意为苦涩、猛烈，exacerbare 就是把东西弄得更苦，所以这个名词最先指病情转向更凶的那一刻。

senses.title: An increase in the severity of a problem
senses.definition: the act of making a problem, a conflict, or a bad situation worse
senses.definitionCN: 使问题、冲突或糟糕局面变得更严重的行为或过程
senses.example: Poverty is both a result and an exacerbation of the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 贫困既是危机的结果，也是危机的加剧因素。
senses.why: The medical image spread outward: any condition that can be made bitter can be made worse, so the noun came to name the sharpening of social and political troubles.
senses.whyCN: 医学意象向外扩散：凡是可以变「苦」的状况都可以被弄得更糟，于是这个名词也指社会与政治困境的加剧。

senses.title: The act of irritating or provoking
senses.definition: the act of making a person angry or irritated
senses.definitionCN: 使某人生气或恼怒的行为
senses.example: His calm questions were an exacerbation rather than a comfort.
senses.exampleCN: 他平静的追问与其说是安慰，不如说是激怒。
senses.why: The Latin verb also meant to provoke, because bitterness was felt as a sting, and the noun kept that older sense of pricking someone into anger.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词还含「挑动」义，因为苦涩被感受为一种刺；名词保留了更早的「刺人发怒」这一层。

senses.title: A countable flare-up episode
senses.definition: a distinct episode in which symptoms flare up and then settle again
senses.definitionCN: 症状突然发作、随后又平复的一次独立病程
senses.example: She recorded three exacerbations in the past year.
senses.exampleCN: 她记录下去年有三次急性加重。
senses.why: Doctors needed to count these events, so the noun moved from an abstract worsening to a single attack, and the plural marks one episode at a time.
senses.whyCN: 医生需要清点这类事件，名词便从抽象的「恶化」转为一次具体的发作，复数正指一次一次单独的发作。

intro.en: Exacerbation comes from Latin acerbus, bitter or harsh, through the verb exacerbare, to make worse or to provoke.
intro.cn: exacerbation 源自拉丁语 acerbus（苦涩、猛烈），经由动词 exacerbare（使恶化、激怒）而来。

items.en: Acerbus means harsh, bitter, or sour, and its sharper cousin acer means keen or cutting.
items.cn: acerbus 意为猛烈、苦涩、酸；它更尖利的近亲 acer 意为锐利、锋利的。

items.en: The verb exacerbare joins ex- to acerbus and means to make harsh, to aggravate, or to provoke.
items.cn: 动词 exacerbare 由 ex- 与 acerbus 合成，意为使变苦、加重或激怒。

items.en: The action noun exacerbatio names the making worse of a condition or of a temper.
items.cn: 动作名词 exacerbatio 指病情或情绪的加重。

items.en: Medical writing in French carries exacerbation forward as a term for a graver turn of illness.
items.cn: 法语医学文献把 exacerbation 传下去，用作病情转向更重的术语。

items.en: English takes the word as a learned medical noun for the sharpening of a disease.
items.cn: 英语接受了这个词，把它当作表示病情加重的学术医学名词。

items.en: Modern usage widens it to problems, conflicts, and countable attacks of illness.
items.cn: 现代用法把它扩展到问题、冲突，以及可数的病情发作。

note.en: Exacerbation sits in the bitter family of acerbus, beside the verb exacerbate, and near the plain worsening words.
note.cn: exacerbation 属于 acerbus 的「苦涩」词族，与动词 exacerbate 同根，也与平实的「恶化」类词相邻。

entries.definition: to make a bad situation or feeling worse
entries.definitionCN: 使糟糕的局面或情绪变得更糟
言辞尖酸刻薄的；同出「苦涩」词根
极度恼火——与 exacerbation 只是拼写相近，词源不同（来自 asper「粗糙」）

entries.definition: the act of making something worse
the process of becoming worse in quality or condition
entries.definitionCN: 质量或状况变坏的过程

entries.definition: a sudden burst of a disease or of anger
entries.definitionCN: 疾病的突然发作；怒气的突然爆发

normalIntro.en: Exacerbation keeps the Latin taste of bitterness: whatever is exacerbated has been made harsher.
normalIntro.cn: exacerbation 保留着拉丁语「苦涩」的味道：被加剧的东西都变得更凶了。

normal.en: Acute exacerbation is a fixed medical phrase for a sudden flare-up.
normal.cn: acute exacerbation 是固定医学说法，指突然的急性加重。

normal.en: Exacerbate is the verb, while exasperate is a different word with a different root.
normal.cn: exacerbate 是动词，exasperate 则是另一个词，词根并不相同。

normal.en: The prefix ex- pushes the meaning outward, so the condition breaks out worse.
normal.cn: 前缀 ex- 把意义向外推，于是病情「爆」得更凶。

normal.en: Planners speak of exacerbating traffic problems, meaning the jams get worse.
normal.cn: 规划者会说「加剧交通问题」，意思就是堵得更厉害。

normal.en: Hospitals count exacerbations, so the plural is common in case reports.
normal.cn: 医院会统计发作次数，所以复数形式在病例报告中很常见。

abstract.en: Picture one bitter drop stirred into clear water until every sip turns harsh.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴苦汁搅进清水，每一口都变得更苦。

abstract.en: Imagine a hairline crack in a dam widening as the water presses on it.
abstract.cn: 想象堤坝上一道细缝在水压下越裂越宽。

abstract.en: Feel a splinter under the skin: the more you touch it, the angrier the spot grows.
abstract.cn: 想象皮肤下扎了一根刺，越碰那处越发红发火。

examples.en: The heat wave brought an exacerbation of her breathing problems.
examples.cn: 热浪使她的呼吸问题加重了。

examples.en: Poverty is both a result and an exacerbation of the crisis.
examples.cn: 贫困既是危机的结果，也是危机的加剧因素。

examples.en: Doctors counted four exacerbations during the winter.
examples.cn: 医生统计出冬季有四次急性加重。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「挨个撒盐」——读起来像挨个往伤口撒盐，越撒越疼，就是「恶化、激怒」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外、加强）+ acerbus（苦涩、猛烈）→ 动词 exacerbare（使更苦、激怒）→ 名词 exacerbatio → 英语 exacerbation，核心义「把状况弄得更苦更凶」。

sensesIntro.en: Exacerbation starts as the medical worsening of a disease, widens to any problem made worse, keeps the older sense of provocation, and ends as a countable flare-up.
sensesIntro.cn: exacerbation 先是医学上病情的加重，再扩展到任何问题的恶化，又保留更早的「激怒」义，最后成为可数的一次发作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one bitter drop stirred into clear water until it turns harsh.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴苦汁搅进清水，直到整杯变苦。

branches.en: A disease turning worse is the medical core of the word.
branches.cn: 病情转为更重，是这个词的医学核心义。

branches.en: Any bad situation can be made harsher, which is the widened sense.
branches.cn: 任何糟糕局面都能被弄得更凶，这是扩展后的义项。

branches.en: The old sense of pricking someone into anger survives beside it.
branches.cn: 「刺人发怒」的旧义一直与它并存。

branches.en: A countable attack is one concrete turn for the worse.
branches.cn: 可数的一次发作，就是一次具体的恶化。

branches.en: A worsened problem and a provoked person are both things made bitter.
branches.cn: 被加剧的问题与被激怒的人，都是被弄「苦」了的对象。

intro.en: Exacerbation is built from the Latin prefix ex-, the root acerbus, bitter, and the noun suffix -ation.
intro.cn: exacerbation 由拉丁语前缀 ex-、词根 acerbus（苦涩）与名词后缀 -ation 组合而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin acerbus means harsh or bitter, and exacerbare means to make harsh or to provoke.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 acerbus 意为苦涩、猛烈，exacerbare 意为使变苦、激怒。

items.example: The prefix ex- intensifies the bitterness.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 加强了「苦」的程度。

items.example: Acerbus describes a sharp and bitter taste.
items.exampleCN: acerbus 描述尖锐苦涩的味道。

items.example: Acer is the sharper cousin of acerbus.
items.exampleCN: acer 是 acerbus 更尖利的近亲。
exacerbare 由 ex- 与 acerbus 合成。

items.example: Exacerbatio is the Latin action noun.
items.exampleCN: exacerbatio 是拉丁语的动作名词。

items.example: The suffix -ation builds a process noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成表示过程的名词。

items.example: Do not confuse it with exasperate.
items.exampleCN: 注意不要把它与 exasperate 混淆。

items.example: Exacerbating factors keep the disease active.
items.exampleCN: 加重因素让疾病持续活动。

items.example: Exasperate comes from asper, rough, not from acerbus.
items.exampleCN: exasperate 来自 asper（粗糙），并非来自 acerbus。

items.example: Acerbic wit shares the bitter root.
items.exampleCN: acerbic 的尖刻共享「苦」这个词根。

definition_en: completely correct and precise
core_image: 一把刻度清晰到毫米的尺子
scene: 木匠量了两次，才在木板上画下精确的切割线。The carpenter measured twice before drawing the exact cutting line on the board.
sceneCN: 这里 exact 是「精确的」（第 1 个义项：每个细节都完全正确）；句意：木匠量了两次，才在木板上画下精确的切割线。

senses.title: Completely correct
senses.definition: completely correct in every detail
senses.definitionCN: 每个细节都完全正确
senses.example: The exact time is ten past five.
senses.exampleCN: 确切时间是五点十分。
senses.why: Exact comes from Latin exigere, to weigh precisely.
senses.whyCN: exact 源自拉丁语 exigere（精确称量）。

senses.title: Strict
senses.definition: demanding great care and accuracy
senses.definitionCN: 要求高度细致准确
senses.example: The exact rules must be followed.
senses.exampleCN: 必须遵守严格的规定。
senses.why: Precise measurement becomes strict demand.
senses.whyCN: 精确的衡量变成严格的要求。

senses.title: To demand
senses.definition: to demand and obtain something
senses.definitionCN: 索取并得到某物
senses.example: The teacher exacted an apology from the class.
senses.exampleCN: 老师要求全班道歉。
senses.why: The verb keeps the old sense of demanding payment.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了索取偿付的旧义。

intro.en: Exact comes from Latin exactus, past participle of exigere, to drive out or weigh.
intro.cn: exact 源自拉丁语 exactus，是 exigere（驱出、称量）的过去分词。

items.en: Agere means to drive or do.
items.cn: agere 意为驱动或做。

items.en: Exigere means to drive out or weigh.
items.cn: exigere 意为驱出或称量。

items.en: Exactus means precise or exacted.
items.cn: exactus 意为精确的或被索取的。

items.en: Exact first describes precise measurement.
items.cn: exact 最初描述精确的测量。

items.en: It also means strict or demanding.
items.cn: 它也指严格或苛求的。

note.en: Exact stresses full correctness; precise stresses fine detail.
note.cn: exact 强调完全正确；precise 强调细节精细。

normalIntro.en: Exact is a ruler marked down to the smallest line.
normalIntro.cn: exact 是一把刻度细到最小格的尺子。

normal.en: Exact time means the precise hour and minute.
normal.cn: exact time 意为确切的小时和分钟。

normal.en: Exact words means the very words used.
normal.cn: exact words 意为原原本本的话。

normal.en: To be exact means to speak precisely.
normal.cn: to be exact 意为确切地说。

normal.en: An exact match fits perfectly.
normal.cn: an exact match 完全吻合。

normal.en: Compare precise: exact stresses no error, precise stresses fine detail.
normal.cn: 对比 precise：exact 强调无误差，precise 强调细节精细。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler with marks down to a millimeter.
abstract.cn: 想象一把刻度细到毫米的尺子。

abstract.en: Imagine two puzzle pieces fitting without a gap.
abstract.cn: 想象两块拼图严丝合缝。

abstract.en: Think of a key that turns only in one lock.
abstract.cn: 想象一把只在一把锁里转动的钥匙。

examples.en: Can you give me the exact date?
examples.cn: 你能告诉我确切的日期吗？

examples.en: Those were his exact words.
examples.cn: 那就是他的原话。

examples.en: The work demands exact measurements.
examples.cn: 这项工作要求精确的测量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「exact」读起来短促干脆——像尺子一下卡到位，分毫不差。

root: 拉丁语 exigere（称量、要求）→ exactus（精确的）→ exact，核心义「量得准、要求严」。

sensesIntro.en: Exact starts with complete correctness, extends to strict demands, and keeps a verb sense of demanding.
sensesIntro.cn: exact 从完全正确开始，延伸到严格要求，还保留索取的动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler marked down to a millimeter.
core.cn: 核心意象：刻度细到毫米的尺子。

branches.en: Complete correctness is the core.
branches.cn: 完全正确是核心含义。

branches.en: Precision can become strictness.
branches.cn: 精确可以变成严格。

branches.en: The verb means to demand.
branches.cn: 动词意为强求。

branches.en: A measured standard and a strict rule meet.
branches.cn: 精确标准与严格规则相遇。

branches.en: Demanding payment and exact measuring share a root.
branches.cn: 索取与精确称量共享同一个词根。

intro.en: Exact joins ex-, out, to the Latin root ag, to drive.
intro.cn: exact 由 ex-（出）与拉丁词根 ag（驱动）组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin exigere is the direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 exigere 是直接来源。

definition_en: to describe something as bigger or better than it is
core_image: 一个小水坑被画成一片汪洋
scene: 他总爱夸大自己的经历，把一次小旅行说成冒险。He always tends to exaggerate his experiences, turning a short trip into an adventure.
sceneCN: 这里 exaggerate 是「夸大」（第 1 个义项：把事情说得比实际更大）；句意：他总爱夸大自己的经历，把一次小旅行说成冒险。

senses.title: Making too much
senses.definition: to make something seem larger or better
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物显得更大或更好
senses.example: She exaggerated the size of the fish.
senses.exampleCN: 她夸大了那条鱼的大小。
senses.why: Ex- out and aggerare to pile up give the image of piling on.
senses.whyCN: ex-（出）与 aggerare（堆积）构成往上堆的意象。

senses.title: Overstating a feeling
senses.definition: to say something is stronger than it is
senses.definitionCN: 把某种感受说得过强
senses.example: He exaggerated his pain to get sympathy.
senses.exampleCN: 他为了博取同情夸大了疼痛。
senses.why: The same piling up applies to feelings.
senses.whyCN: 同样的堆积也适用于感受。

senses.title: To make too large
senses.definition: to make something larger than normal
senses.definitionCN: 使某物大于正常
senses.example: The wide lens exaggerates the distance.
senses.exampleCN: 广角镜头会夸大距离感。
senses.why: The visual sense keeps the literal idea of enlargement.
senses.whyCN: 视觉含义保留了放大的字面意思。

intro.en: Exaggerate comes from Latin exaggerare, to heap up.
intro.cn: exaggerate 源自拉丁语 exaggerare（堆高）。

items.en: Agger means a heap.
items.cn: agger 意为堆。

items.en: Aggerare means to heap up.
items.cn: aggerare 意为堆起。

items.en: Exaggerare means to pile up.
items.cn: exaggerare 意为堆积。

items.en: Exaggerate first means to heap up.
items.cn: exaggerate 最初意为堆高。

items.en: It means to overstate.
items.cn: 它逐渐指夸大其词。

note.en: Exaggerate is to describe too strongly; overstate is its formal twin.
note.cn: exaggerate 指描述得过头；overstate 是它更正式的同义词。

entries.definition: to make a number or claim seem larger

normalIntro.en: Exaggerate is piling extra words on a small fact.
normalIntro.cn: exaggerate 是在小事实上一层层堆词。

normal.en: Exaggerate the danger means make it seem worse.
normal.cn: exaggerate the danger 意为把危险说得更严重。

normal.en: Exaggerate the size means claim it is bigger.
normal.cn: exaggerate the size 意为声称尺寸更大。

normal.en: Grossly exaggerate means overstate very much.
normal.cn: grossly exaggerate 意为严重夸大。

normal.en: Without exaggerating means speaking plainly.
normal.cn: without exaggerating 意为毫不夸张地说。

normal.en: Compare overstate: exaggerate is everyday, overstate is formal.
normal.cn: 对比 overstate：exaggerate 更日常，overstate 更正式。

abstract.en: Picture a small puddle drawn as a wide sea.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小水坑被画成一片汪洋。

abstract.en: Imagine a shadow at sunset stretching far beyond its owner.
abstract.cn: 想象日落时影子被拉得远远超过本人。

abstract.en: Think of a story that grows with every telling.
abstract.cn: 想象一个每讲一次就变大的故事。

examples.en: Don't exaggerate the difficulties.
examples.cn: 不要夸大困难。

examples.en: The report exaggerates the benefits of the plan.
examples.cn: 报告夸大了计划的好处。

examples.en: He tends to exaggerate when he is nervous.
examples.cn: 他紧张时容易夸大其词。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）＋ agger（堆）」——往事实外面不断堆东西，就是夸大。

root: 拉丁语 exaggerare（堆高）＝ ex-（出）＋ aggerare（堆积）→ exaggerate，核心义「越堆越高、言过其实」。

sensesIntro.en: Exaggerate means to make a fact seem larger, to overstate a feeling, and even to enlarge an image.
sensesIntro.cn: exaggerate 指把事实说得更大、把感受说过头，也可指放大图像。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small puddle drawn as a wide sea.
core.cn: 核心意象：小水坑被画成汪洋。

branches.en: Piling onto a fact is the core.
branches.cn: 在事实上一层层堆积是核心。

branches.en: Feelings can be overdone too.
branches.cn: 感受也能被夸大。

branches.en: Images can be enlarged as well.
branches.cn: 图像也能被放大。

branches.en: Facts and feelings both grow in the telling.
branches.cn: 事实与感受都在讲述中变大。

branches.en: Words and lenses both enlarge.
branches.cn: 言语与镜头都在放大。

intro.en: Exaggerate joins ex-, out, to the Latin root agger, a heap.
intro.cn: exaggerate 由 ex-（出）与拉丁词根 agger（堆）组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin exaggerare is the direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 exaggerare 是直接来源。

definition_en: a feeling of great joy, or the act of raising someone in rank or praising them highly
core_image: 两双手把一个人高高举起，众人都要仰头看
scene: 毕业典礼上，她把帽子抛向空中，脸上全是压不住的狂喜。A wave of exaltation swept over the graduates as the music began.
sceneCN: 这里 exaltation 是「兴高采烈、狂喜」（第 1 个义项：情绪被举高）；句意：音乐响起时，一阵狂喜掠过毕业生们。

derivatives.zh: 由名词去后缀 -ation 还原的动词，义为「提升；颂扬；使兴奋」
动词加 -ed 构成的形容词，义为「地位高的；崇高的；兴奋的」
动词加 -ing 构成的形容词，义为「令人振奋的；使人高尚的」

senses.title: A feeling of intense joy
senses.definition: a feeling of great joy and excitement that lifts the mind above its ordinary mood
senses.definitionCN: 极度喜悦与兴奋，心神被抬到日常情绪之上
senses.example: A sense of exaltation filled the hall as the choir rose.
senses.exampleCN: 合唱团起立时，一种狂喜充满了大厅。
senses.why: Latin altus means high, so a lifted mind is the source image, and the noun names that upward surge of feeling.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 altus 意为「高」，心神被举高正是这个词的画面来源，名词便指情绪向上涌起的状态。

senses.title: The act of raising to a high rank
senses.definition: the act of raising a person to a higher position, honour, or dignity
senses.definitionCN: 把人提升到更高职位、荣誉或地位的行为
senses.example: His exaltation to the chairmanship surprised no one.
senses.exampleCN: 他被擢升为主席，谁也不感到意外。
senses.why: The verb exaltare means literally to lift up, so applied to persons the noun names the act of placing someone on higher ground.
senses.whyCN: 动词 exaltare 字面就是「举起来」，用在人身上，名词便指把人放到更高位置的这个动作。

senses.title: Praise or glorification
senses.definition: the act of praising someone or something highly, especially in worship
senses.definitionCN: 高度赞扬某人或某物，尤指在宗教崇拜中
senses.example: The psalm ends in the exaltation of the divine name.
senses.exampleCN: 这首圣诗以颂扬神名作结。
senses.why: To lift a name up in words is to praise it, so the same upward image moved from physical height into speech and worship.
senses.whyCN: 用言语把名字举高就是颂扬，同一个「向上」的意象于是从身体的高度转移到言说与崇拜里。

senses.title: A state of lofty dignity
senses.definition: the condition of being elevated in dignity, purity, or spiritual worth
senses.definitionCN: 在尊严、纯净或精神价值上处于高处的状态
senses.example: The old hymns speak of the exaltation of the soul after death.
senses.exampleCN: 古老的赞美诗谈到灵魂在死后得到的升华。
senses.why: Because height was read as worth, the noun also names a lasting elevated condition rather than a single act or a passing feeling.
senses.whyCN: 因为「高」被读作「贵」，这个名词也指一种持久的高贵状态，而不只是一次举动或一阵情绪。

intro.en: Exaltation comes from Latin altus, high, through the verb exaltare, to lift up.
intro.cn: exaltation 源自拉丁语 altus（高），经由动词 exaltare（举高）而来。

items.en: Altus means high or lofty, and is generally taken as growing from alere, to nourish, in the sense of grown tall.
items.cn: altus 意为高的、崇高的，一般认为它源自 alere（养育），取「已经长高」之意。

items.en: The verb exaltare joins ex- to altus and means to lift up or to raise.
items.cn: 动词 exaltare 由 ex- 与 altus 合成，意为举起、抬高。

items.en: The noun exaltatio names a lifting up, whether of a body, a rank, or a mood.
items.cn: 名词 exaltatio 指举起，可以是身体、地位或情绪上的举起。

items.en: Old French exaltation keeps both the religious and the social senses alive.
items.cn: 古法语 exaltation 同时让宗教与社会两方面的含义延续下来。

items.en: English adopts the word for raising in rank, for praise, and for lifted feeling.
items.cn: 英语采用这个词，用来表示提升地位、颂扬与情绪高涨。

items.en: In modern use the emotional sense of elation is the most common one.
items.cn: 在现代用法中，表示情绪高涨的「狂喜」义最为常见。

note.en: Exaltation belongs to the high family of altus, beside the verb exalt, and near the words for joy, raising, and praise.
note.cn: exaltation 属于 altus 的「高」词族，与动词 exalt 同根，并与表示喜悦、提升、赞扬的词相邻。

entries.definition: to raise in rank or to praise highly
high in rank, noble, or filled with joy
entries.definitionCN: 地位高的；崇高的；满心欢喜的
欢腾与得意——与 exaltation 只是拼写相近，词源不同（来自 exsultare「跳起」）

entries.definition: a mood of high spirits and joy
the act of raising something or the state of being raised
the act of praising something as glorious

normalIntro.en: Exaltation carries the Latin altus, high: something in the mind or in rank has been lifted.
normalIntro.cn: exaltation 带着拉丁语 altus（高）的底子：不是心神被举高，就是地位被举高。

normal.en: Exalt and exaltation share the Latin altus, which means high.
normal.cn: exalt 与 exaltation 共享拉丁语 altus，意为「高」。

normal.en: Altitude comes from the same altus, so height ties the whole family together.
normal.cn: altitude 也来自同一个 altus，高度把整个词族串在一起。

normal.en: Exultation looks alike but comes from exsultare, to leap up.
normal.cn: exultation 形似，却来自 exsultare（跳起来）。

normal.en: In worship, exaltation names the lifting of a name in praise.
normal.cn: 在崇拜中，exaltation 指把某个名字高举颂扬。

normal.en: Raise is the plain verb, while exalt is the literary and religious one.
normal.cn: raise 是平实的动词，exalt 则更文学、更宗教。

abstract.en: Picture a kite pulled up by a gust until it rides above the rooftops.
abstract.cn: 想象风筝被一阵风拉起，一直升到屋顶之上。

abstract.en: See a hand lifting a young scholar onto a higher step of a stone stair.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把年轻学者托上石阶更高的一级。

abstract.en: Hear a crowd lift one name high above all the noise.
abstract.cn: 想象人群把一个名字高高举过所有喧哗。

examples.en: The crowd rose in a mood of pure exaltation.
examples.cn: 人群起身，沉浸在纯粹的狂喜之中。

examples.en: His exaltation to the rank of master came after thirty years of service.
examples.cn: 在服务三十年后，他被擢升为大师。

examples.en: The hymn is a song of exaltation, not of complaint.
examples.cn: 这首圣诗是一曲颂扬，而不是抱怨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱个高台」——读起来像「爱个高台」，人往高台上一站，心就飘起来，既是被提升也是狂喜；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外、向上）+ altus（高，一般认为源自 alere「养育、长高」）→ 动词 exaltare（举高、抬高）→ 名词 exaltatio → 英语 exaltation，核心义「把人或心举到高处」。

sensesIntro.en: Exaltation moves from a lifted feeling of joy, to the act of raising someone in rank, to praise, and finally to a lasting state of lofty dignity.
sensesIntro.cn: exaltation 从被举高的喜悦，走到把某人提升的举动，再到颂扬，最后指一种持久的高贵状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands lifting a person until the crowd must look up.
core.cn: 核心意象：两双手把一个人举起，众人只能抬头看。

branches.en: Joy is the mind lifted above its usual level.
branches.cn: 喜悦就是心神被举到平常水平之上。

branches.en: Rank is the body placed on a higher step.
branches.cn: 地位就是把身体放上更高的一级台阶。

branches.en: Praise is a name lifted in speech and song.
branches.cn: 赞扬就是在言说与歌唱里把名字举高。

branches.en: Dignity is height that has become permanent.
branches.cn: 高贵是被固定下来的高度。

branches.en: Singing praise often produces the lifted feeling itself.
branches.cn: 唱颂本身常常就会带来那种被举起的感觉。

intro.en: Exaltation combines the Latin prefix ex-, the root altus, high, and the noun suffix -ation.
intro.cn: exaltation 由拉丁语前缀 ex-、词根 altus（高）与名词后缀 -ation 组合而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin altus means high or deep, and exaltare means to raise or to lift up.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 altus 意为高的、深的，exaltare 意为举高、抬高。

items.example: The prefix ex- turns height into a lifting.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 把「高」变成了「举起」。
altus 描述高耸挺立之物。

items.example: Altus is generally taken to grow from alere.
items.exampleCN: 一般认为 altus 源自 alere。
exaltare 由 ex- 与 altus 合成。

items.example: Exaltatio is the Latin action noun.
items.exampleCN: exaltatio 是拉丁语的动作名词。

items.example: The suffix -ation builds a state noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成表示状态的名词。

items.example: Exalt is the shorter English verb.
items.exampleCN: exalt 是更简短的英语动词。

items.example: Exultation comes from exsultare, to leap up.

definition_en: to look at something closely or test someone's knowledge
core_image: 医生俯身查看病人的影像片
scene: 医院里，医生对着影像片仔细查看每一处细节。The doctor examined the films slowly and carefully.
sceneCN: 这里 examine 是「检查」（第 1 个义项：仔细查看以了解状况）；句意：医院里，医生对着影像片仔细查看每一处细节。

senses.title: Looking closely
senses.definition: to look at something carefully to learn about it
senses.definitionCN: 仔细观察某物以了解情况
senses.example: The doctor examined her eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 医生检查了她的眼睛。
senses.why: The verb points a close look at one thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词指向对某一事物的仔细查看。

senses.title: Testing knowledge
senses.definition: to test what someone knows
senses.definitionCN: 测试某人掌握的知识
senses.example: The teacher examined the class in grammar.
senses.exampleCN: 老师对全班进行了语法考试。
senses.why: Testing is a way of weighing knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 测试是称量知识的一种方式。

senses.title: Questioning formally
senses.definition: to question someone officially
senses.definitionCN: 正式向某人提问
senses.example: The police examined the witness for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 警方盘问了证人一小时。
senses.why: Questions dig out facts one by one.
senses.whyCN: 提问把事实一条条挖出来。

intro.en: Examine comes from Latin exigere, to weigh or drive out, through examen.
intro.cn: examine 经由 examen 源自拉丁语 exigere（称量、驱出）。

items.en: Exigere means to weigh or drive out.
items.cn: exigere 意为称量或驱出。

items.en: Examen is the tongue of a balance.
items.cn: examen 是天平的指针。

items.en: Old French examiner means to question.
items.cn: 古法语 examiner 意为盘问。

items.en: English examine first means to inspect closely.
items.cn: 英语 examine 最初指仔细查看。

items.en: Doctors now examine patients as a daily act.
items.cn: 如今医生每天都为病人做检查。

note.en: Examine is the verb; exam and examination are the nouns it stands behind.
note.cn: examine 是动词，exam 与 examination 是与之对应的名词。

entries.definition: a short word for an examination
a test or a careful check
to make sure something is right

normalIntro.en: To examine is to put something on the scales.
normalIntro.cn: examine 就是把某物放到天平上。

normal.en: An examiner is the person who examines.
normal.cn: examiner 就是进行 examine 的人。

normal.en: Examine the evidence before you judge.
normal.cn: 下判断前先审查证据。

normal.en: Doctors examine patients with care.
normal.cn: 医生仔细检查病人。

normal.en: Cross-examine means question again and again.
normal.cn: cross-examine 意为反复盘问。

normal.en: Examine is the verb behind examination.
normal.cn: examine 是 examination 背后的动词。

abstract.en: Picture hands turning a stone to see every side.
abstract.cn: 想象双手转动石头查看每一面。

abstract.en: Imagine a scale tipping under a question.
abstract.cn: 想象天平在一个问题下倾斜。

abstract.en: Think of a torch sweeping a dark room.
abstract.cn: 想象手电扫过黑暗的房间。

examples.en: The committee examined every report.
examples.cn: 委员会审查了每一份报告。

examples.en: She examined the map before the trip.
examples.cn: 出发前她仔细看了地图。

examples.en: The judge examined the witness calmly.
examples.cn: 法官平静地盘问证人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）＋ amine」——把问题一条条挖出来，就是检查与考查。

root: 拉丁语 exigere（称量；驱出）→ examen（天平指针）→ examine，核心义「把事物放上天平逐一查看」。

sensesIntro.en: Examine means to look closely, to test knowledge, or to question officially.
sensesIntro.cn: examine 意为仔细查看、考查知识或正式盘问。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone turned in the hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：在手中转动的石头。

branches.en: Turning the stone is the close look.
branches.cn: 转动石头就是仔细查看。

branches.en: Testing puts the learner on the scales.
branches.cn: 考查把学习者放上天平。

branches.en: Questions press the witness for facts.
branches.cn: 提问向证人追问事实。

branches.en: Both looking and testing are acts of weighing.
branches.cn: 查看与考查都是称量的动作。

branches.en: A test and an interrogation both ask questions.
branches.cn: 考试与审问都在提问。

intro.en: Examine goes back to Latin exigere, to weigh or drive out.
intro.cn: examine 可追溯到拉丁语 exigere（称量、驱出）。

latinIntro.en: Ex- plus agere, to drive, forms exigere, and examen follows.
latinIntro.cn: ex- 加 agere（驱动）构成 exigere，随后又有了 examen。

items.example: The examiner sat at the front.

items.exampleCN: exam 省略了长长的词尾。

latinEntries.example: Exigere is the source of examine.
latinEntries.exampleCN: exigere 是 examine 的来源。
examen 把称量与测试联系起来。

definition_zh: 激怒；使恼火；使失去耐心；加剧（书面，指病情或麻烦）
definition_en: to make someone extremely annoyed and frustrated, especially by repeated provocation
core_image: 一块粗糙的石头反复摩擦绳子，把绳子一点点磨起毛
scene: 深夜的会议室里，同一个问题被反复追问，主管终于压不住火气。After the third round of questions, the same answer began to exasperate the whole team.
sceneCN: 这里 exasperate 是「激怒、使恼火」（第 1 个义项：使人非常生气）；句意：问到第三轮时，同样的回答开始让整个团队恼火。

pos.zh: 激怒；使恼火；使失去耐心

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -tion 构成名词，义为「恼怒；愤懑」
现在分词转形容词，义为「令人恼火的」
过去分词转形容词，义为「被激怒的；又气又无奈的」
形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「恼火地」

senses.title: To make someone very angry
senses.definition: to make a person extremely annoyed, often so that the anger shows in the voice or face
senses.definitionCN: 使人极为恼火，往往气得在声音或脸色上表露出来
senses.example: Slow traffic and endless forms exasperate most drivers.
senses.exampleCN: 缓慢的车流和没完没了的表格让大多数司机恼火。
senses.why: Latin asper means rough, and exasperare meant to make a surface rough; to exasperate a person is to roughen the temper until it turns harsh.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 asper 意为「粗糙」，exasperare 本义是「使表面变粗糙」；激怒一个人，就是把他的脾气磨粗，直到语气变硬。

senses.title: To wear down the patience of someone
senses.titleCN: 使失去耐心；使无可奈何
senses.definition: to exhaust the patience of a person through many small repeated irritations rather than one large offence
senses.definitionCN: 不是一次大的冒犯，而是许多小事反复消耗掉一个人的耐心
senses.example: The endless questions of the child at bedtime exasperated his tired mother.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子临睡前没完没了的问题，让疲惫的母亲失去了耐心。
senses.why: The verb pictures a process rather than a blow, so the object is not struck once but worn thin until patience runs out.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词描绘的是一段过程而不是一次打击，所以对象不是被击中一次，而是被磨薄到耐心耗尽。

senses.title: To be left helplessly annoyed
senses.titleCN: 被弄得又气又无奈（多用被动）
senses.definition: used in the passive, to describe a settled state of frustrated anger with no easy outlet
senses.definitionCN: 多用于被动语态，描述一种找不到出口、已经定型的恼怒与无奈
senses.example: She was exasperated by the refusal of the council to answer her letters.
senses.exampleCN: 市政会始终不回复她的信，她被弄得又气又无奈。
senses.why: In the passive the participle names the end point of the roughening, so the sentence reports a state that has already set in, not an act in progress.
senses.whyCN: 在被动语态里，分词指的是「磨粗」这一过程的结果，所以句子陈述的是一种已经形成的心态，而不是正在进行的动作。

senses.title: To make a bad condition worse
senses.titleCN: 加剧；使（病情、麻烦）恶化（书面，少见）
senses.definition: to intensify an illness, a wound, or a difficulty; a formal and now uncommon use
senses.definitionCN: 使疾病、伤口或困难加重；书面语用法，如今已少见
senses.example: Cold winds exasperated the old wound in his leg.
senses.exampleCN: 冷风让他腿上的旧伤更加难熬。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer of the image: roughening a surface makes a sore place worse, so the same verb once meant to aggravate a disease.
senses.whyCN: 这是意象中最古老的一层：把表面磨粗会让原本疼痛的地方更难受，所以这个动词过去也能表示「使病情加重」。

intro.en: Exasperate comes from Latin exasperare, to make rough, built from ex- and asper, rough; English took the verb in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: exasperate 来自拉丁语 exasperare（使变粗糙），由 ex- 与 asper（粗糙）构成；英语在十六世纪引入这个动词。

items.en: Asper is a Latin adjective meaning rough, harsh, or uneven.
items.cn: asper 是拉丁语形容词，意为粗糙的、严厉的、不平整的。

items.en: Ex- adds the idea of thoroughly or out, and asperare means to make rough.
items.cn: 前缀 ex- 加上「彻底、向外」的意思，asperare 意为使变粗糙。

items.en: Exasperare means to roughen and, in transferred use, to provoke or irritate.
items.cn: exasperare 意为使粗糙，引申用法则是挑动、激怒。

items.en: English borrows the verb in the 1500s with the sense of provoking anger.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个动词，义为挑起怒火。

items.en: Later English keeps both the everyday sense of annoying and the older medical sense of worsening a condition.
items.cn: 后来的英语同时保留了「使人恼火」的日常义和「使病情加重」的古老医学义。

note.en: Exasperate belongs to the rough family of asper, and stands at the strong end of the anger words.
note.cn: exasperate 属于 asper（粗糙）这个词族，在表示「生气」的词里处于强烈的一端。

entries.definition: the feeling of being extremely annoyed
to make someone a little angry

normalIntro.en: Exasperate keeps the Latin word for rough, so the picture is a temper rubbed the wrong way.
normalIntro.cn: exasperate 保留了拉丁语里「粗糙」这个词，所以画面是被逆向摩擦的脾气。

normal.en: Asper in Latin means rough, and exasperate keeps that roughness inside the anger.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 asper 意为粗糙，exasperate 把这份粗糙留在了怒火里。

normal.en: Add the prefix ex- and the verb moves from making rough to making angry.
normal.cn: 加上前缀 ex-，动词就从「使粗糙」走到「使生气」。

normal.en: The noun is exasperation, the worn-out feeling left after repeated annoyance.
normal.cn: 名词是 exasperation，指反复被烦之后留下的那种疲惫的恼怒。

normal.en: Say exasperated by, exasperated at, or exasperated with to name the cause.
normal.cn: 说 exasperated by、exasperated at 或 exasperated with 都能点出原因。

normal.en: Compare irritate: irritate is milder, exasperate is the worn-down stronger end.
normal.cn: 对比 irritate：irritate 较轻，exasperate 是被磨到尽头、更强烈的那一端。

abstract.en: Picture a rough stone dragging across a rope until the fibres stand up.
abstract.cn: 想象一块粗石在绳子上拖过，直到纤维全都竖起来。

abstract.en: Imagine a tap dripping on the same spot all night.
abstract.cn: 想象一个水龙头整夜滴在同一处。

abstract.en: Think of a door that will not open however hard you push.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，无论怎么推都推不开。

examples.en: The constant noise from the building site exasperated the whole street.
examples.cn: 工地不断的噪音让整条街的人都恼火。

examples.en: He was exasperated by the endless delays at the airport.
examples.cn: 机场没完没了的延误把他弄得又气又无奈。

examples.en: Nothing exasperates her more than a meeting with no agenda.
examples.cn: 没有什么比一场没有议程的会议更让她恼火。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一个在死逼」——被人一步步逼到火气上来，就是被激怒；拆开看是 ex 加 asper（粗糙），粗糙的摩擦让人恼火，这一半才是词源线索，谐音部分只是辅助。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外、彻底）+ asper（粗糙）→ exasperare（使粗糙、激怒）→ 拉丁语 exasperatus → 英语 exasperate，核心义「把脾气磨粗糙」。

sensesIntro.en: Exasperate starts as making rough, becomes making angry, then wearing patience thin, then naming a helpless state, and finally worsening a condition.
sensesIntro.cn: exasperate 从「使粗糙」出发，先指使人发火，再指把耐心磨薄，继而指一种无奈的心态，最后指使病情或麻烦加重。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rough stone rubbing a rope until it frays.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块粗糙的石头反复摩擦绳子，直到绳子起毛。

branches.en: Roughness turned against a person is the core sense of open anger.
branches.cn: 把粗糙施加到人身上，就是表露在外的怒火这一核心义。

branches.en: Friction repeated many times wears patience down instead of striking once.
branches.cn: 反复的摩擦不是一次打击，而是把耐心一点点磨掉。

branches.en: The passive result is a settled state of helpless anger.
branches.cn: 被动语态的结果，是一种已经定型的无奈怒火。

branches.en: The old medical use keeps the literal idea of making a sore place rougher.
branches.cn: 古老的医学用法保留了「让疼痛处更粗糙」这一字面意思。

branches.en: Both senses share the same picture of a temper being rubbed the wrong way.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享同一幅画面：脾气被逆向摩擦。

intro.en: Exasperate is built from the Latin prefix ex- and asper, rough, with English suffixes forming the noun and the two adjectives.
intro.cn: exasperate 由拉丁语前缀 ex- 与 asper（粗糙）构成，英语再用后缀造出名词和两个形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin asper means rough, and exasperare means to make rough and, by transfer, to provoke.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 asper 意为粗糙，exasperare 意为使粗糙，引申为挑动、激怒。

items.example: The prefix ex- strengthens the verb.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 加强了动词的语气。
asper 提供粗糙的表面这一意象。

items.example: Asperare turns the adjective into an action.
items.exampleCN: asperare 把这个形容词变成动作。

items.example: Exasperare is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: exasperare 是英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: Exasperatus gives the passive sense of the result.
items.exampleCN: exasperatus 提供表示结果的被动含义。

items.meaningCN: 由拉丁词干构成动词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ate carries the Latin stem into English.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 把拉丁词干带入英语。

items.example: Exasperate keeps the learned tone of the Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: exasperate 保留了拉丁动词的书面语色彩。

items.meaningCN: 由动词构成形容词的词尾

definition_zh: 挖掘；发掘（遗址）；挖出；挖空；揭示（隐藏的事实）
definition_en: to dig out earth or buried material, to hollow out a space, or to bring hidden facts to light
core_image: 一把铲子切入土层，土被抛向一侧，坑底露出一块刻字的石头
scene: 探方里，工作人员先用铲子切开草皮，再把土一筐筐运到筛网旁，坑底露出一块刻字石头。They excavate the trench by hand, removing the soil layer by layer, so that no small find is lost.
sceneCN: 这里 excavate 指「按层挖开遗址」（第 1 个义项：以手工方式挖掘并保留细节）；句意为他们手工挖掘这条探沟，以免任何细小发现被漏掉。可辨识物件：铲子、草皮、土筐、筛网、刻字石头。

pos.zh: 挖掘；发掘；挖出（过去式 excavated，过去分词 excavated，现在分词 excavating）
进行挖掘；（场地等）容易被挖开

senses.title: To dig out earth
senses.definition: to remove soil or rock in order to make a hole, cutting or level
senses.definitionCN: 为形成洞、切口或平面而移走土或岩石
senses.example: They excavate the trench by hand so that no small find is lost.
senses.exampleCN: 他们手工挖掘这条探沟，以免任何细小发现被漏掉。
senses.why: ex- 'out' plus cavare 'to hollow' means the verb is literally 'to hollow out'.
senses.whyCN: ex-「出」加 cavare「挖空」，因此这个动词字面就是「挖空」。

senses.title: To dig an archaeological site
senses.definition: to remove deposits layer by layer in order to expose and record remains
senses.definitionCN: 逐层移去堆积，以暴露并记录遗存
senses.example: Students excavate the floor in squares of one metre.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们按一米方格发掘地面。
senses.why: the verb followed the noun into archaeology and now implies method, not only muscle.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词随名词进入考古学，如今暗示方法，而不只是力气。

senses.title: To dig out an object
senses.definition: to free a buried object by removing the material around it
senses.definitionCN: 通过移走周围材料使埋藏物脱出
senses.example: They excavated the jar without breaking its rim.
senses.exampleCN: 他们挖出陶罐，没有弄破罐口。
senses.why: the object is the goal, and the verb can take it as a direct object.
senses.whyCN: 物件是目标，动词可以把它作直接宾语。

senses.title: To hollow out a space
senses.definition: to form a cavity, tunnel or channel inside a mass
senses.definitionCN: 在实体内部形成腔、隧道或通道
senses.example: Workers excavated a passage through the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 工人穿过山体开凿了一条通道。
senses.why: here the verb creates empty space rather than exposing something.
senses.whyCN: 这里动词创造空处，而不是暴露某物。

senses.title: To cut in engineering or geology
senses.definition: to remove material for a foundation, road, canal or mine
senses.definitionCN: 为地基、道路、运河或矿井移走材料
senses.example: The company excavated the slope for the new road.
senses.exampleCN: 公司为新路开挖山坡。
senses.why: the engineering sense is the oldest English use and remains the commonest outside archaeology.
senses.whyCN: 工程义是英语中最早的用法，在考古之外仍最常见。

senses.title: To uncover hidden facts
senses.definition: by extension, to search through records or evidence until what was concealed appears
senses.definitionCN: 引申指翻查记录或证据，直到被掩盖之物显现
senses.example: The reporter excavated the old correspondence.
senses.exampleCN: 记者翻查旧通信，把内情挖了出来。
senses.why: the metaphor treats archives as strata, and the verb keeps its 'remove to reveal' shape.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把档案当作地层，动词保留「移走以显现」的形状。

senses.title: The dental sense
senses.definition: to hollow out decayed tissue from a tooth before filling it
senses.definitionCN: 补牙前把牙上的腐坏组织挖除
senses.example: The dentist excavated the cavity before the filling.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医在填补之前挖除了龋洞。
senses.why: dentistry borrowed the literal sense: a small cavity is hollowed with a small tool.
senses.whyCN: 牙科借用字面义：用小工具把小小的腔挖空。

senses.title: Abstraction: to peel away layers
senses.definition: any process of removing layer after layer until a hidden structure is seen
senses.definitionCN: 层层移除直到看见隐藏结构的任何过程
senses.example: To understand the custom, she excavated its assumptions.
senses.exampleCN: 为了理解这一习俗，她层层挖出它的预设。
senses.why: the deepest sense needs no soil: any covering can be excavated if it can be removed in layers.
senses.whyCN: 最深的一层不需要泥土：任何能被逐层移除的覆盖物都可被「发掘」。

intro.en: Excavate is recorded in English in the late sixteenth century; it may come from the Latin participle excavatus or from the noun excavation, and dictionaries differ. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: excavate 在十六世纪晚期见于英语；它可能来自拉丁过去分词 excavatus，也可能由名词 excavation 派生，辞书说法不一。年代均为约数。

items.en: The past participle excavatus meant 'hollowed out', and it is one plausible source of the English verb.
items.cn: 过去分词 excavatus 意为「被挖空的」，是英语动词的可能来源之一。

items.en: English excavate appears in the late sixteenth century; whether it was taken from the Latin participle or formed from excavation is not settled, so both paths are listed rather than one ruling.
items.cn: 英语 excavate 出现于十六世纪晚期；它是取自拉丁过去分词，还是由 excavation 派生，尚无定论，因此两条路径并列，不作单一判定。

items.en: The first English uses concerned foundations, canals and mines, where the verb meant simply to remove ground.
items.cn: 最早的英语用法涉及地基、运河与矿井，动词只表示移走土方。

items.en: Systematic archaeology in the nineteenth century gave the verb its layer-by-layer, record-keeping sense.
items.cn: 十九世纪系统考古学赋予这个动词逐层、留记录的义项。

items.en: Dentistry applied the verb to the small-scale hollowing of a decayed tooth, preserving the literal image.
items.cn: 牙科把这个动词用于牙体腐坏处的小规模挖除，保留了字面意象。

items.en: Source uncertain (first English date and noun-verb path): dictionaries differ on the earliest use, and the relation between the noun and the verb is reconstructed from citation patterns rather than documented in a single statement.
items.cn: 来源不确定（英语首见年代与名动关系）：辞书对最早的用例说法不一，名词与动词之间的关系是依书证模式重构的，并没有单一文献直接说明。

note.en: Group one holds verbs of digging easily confused with excavate; group two holds verbs of revealing.
note.cn: 第一组是易与 excavate 混淆的挖掘动词；第二组是揭示类动词。

entries.definition: To break and remove ground; it lacks the methodical, recorded sense that excavate carries.
entries.definitionCN: 指破土移土；缺少 excavate 所含的有方法、留记录的意味。

entries.definition: To dig a hole or tunnel, especially as an animal does; the scale is small and the agent often non-human.
entries.definitionCN: 指挖洞或掘隧道，尤指动物所为；规模小，施动者常非人。

entries.definition: To make something empty inside; it shares the cavus image but says nothing about exposing remains.
entries.definitionCN: 指使内部变空；共享 cavus 意象，但不涉及暴露遗存。

entries.definition: To take up mud or objects from a river or seabed; the medium is water, not soil.
entries.definitionCN: 指从河底或海床取泥或取物；介质是水，而非土。

entries.definition: To discover something buried or hidden; it stresses the find rather than the digging method.
entries.definitionCN: 指发现埋藏或隐藏之物；强调发现，而非挖掘方法。

entries.definition: To remove a body from the ground; it is a legal and forensic term, narrower than excavate.
entries.definitionCN: 指从地下取出遗体；是法律与法医术语，比 excavate 窄。

entries.definition: To dig for ore or coal; the aim is extraction, not research.
entries.definitionCN: 指为矿石或煤而挖；目的在开采，而非研究。

entries.definition: To make a long narrow cut in the ground, often for defence or drainage.
entries.definitionCN: 指在地面挖狭长沟，常用于防御或排水。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin pieces, the back-formation and the four settings of the verb.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁成分、逆构过程，以及这个动词的四种场景。

normal.en: ex- 'out' + cavare 'hollow': to hollow out.
normal.cn: ex-「出」+ cavare「挖空」：把东西挖空。

normal.en: The verb is a back-formation from excavation, not a direct Latin loan at first.
normal.cn: 这个动词由 excavation 逆构而来，最初不是直接借自拉丁。

normal.en: The family runs excavate, excavation, excavator, cavity, cave.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 excavate、excavation、excavator、cavity、cave。

normal.en: Four settings: foundations, archaeology, tunnels and teeth.
normal.cn: 四种场景：地基、考古、隧道与牙齿。

normal.en: Typical partners are site, trench, by hand, foundations.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是「遗址」「沟」「手工」与「地基」。

abstract.en: Picture a spade that turns over not soil but assumptions.
abstract.cn: 想象一把铲子翻起的不是土，而是预设。

abstract.en: Picture a floor dug in squares so that nothing is missed.
abstract.cn: 想象地面被划成方格挖掘，以免遗漏。

abstract.en: Picture a hole made on purpose so that something else can be seen.
abstract.cn: 想象故意挖出的一个洞，为的是看见别的东西。

examples.en: Archaeologists excavate slowly when the soil is wet.
examples.cn: 土壤潮湿时，考古学家会缓慢发掘。

examples.en: The crew excavated the old cellar before building the tower.
examples.cn: 在建塔之前，施工队挖开了旧地窖。

examples.en: The dentist excavated the decay and filled the tooth.
examples.cn: 牙医挖除腐坏部分并补好了牙。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）+ cav（洞）+ ate（做）」——把洞挖出来 → 挖掘；发掘

root: 英语 excavate 见于十六世纪晚期，可能来自拉丁过去分词 excavatus，也可能由 excavation 派生，辞书说法不一；excavation 来自拉丁 excavare「挖空」= ex-（出）+ cavare（使空），cavare 源于 cavus「空的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one spade: material is removed. The act becomes plain digging, then archaeological method, then freeing an object, hollowing a passage, engineering, uncovering facts, dental work and finally the peeling of any layers.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一把铲子展开：材料被移走。这个动作先成为普通挖掘，再成为考古方法、取出物件、挖通通道、工程开挖、揭示事实、牙科操作，最后成为任何层层剥离。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spade cutting into soil, earth thrown to one side, a carved stone appearing at the bottom.
core.cn: 核心意象：铲子切入土中，土被抛向一侧，坑底露出一块刻字石头。

branches.en: THE PLAIN CUT: foundations and roads need only removal.
branches.cn: 普通切口：地基与道路只需要移走。

branches.en: METHOD AND OBJECT: careful layers free a find without breaking it.
branches.cn: 方法与物件：细致的分层能在不破坏的情况下取出发现。

branches.en: THE SMALL CAVITY: tunnels and teeth are hollowed by the same image.
branches.cn: 小空腔：隧道与牙齿用同一意象挖空。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: archives become strata and facts become finds.
branches.cn: 比喻：档案成为地层，事实成为出土物。

branches.en: PEELING LAYERS: the deepest sense needs no earth at all.
branches.cn: 剥离层：最深的一层根本不需要泥土。

intro.en: Excavate is a verb made of a Latin prefix and root, with a noun family that keeps the hollow image.
intro.cn: excavate 是由拉丁前缀与词根构成的动词，其名词词族保留「空」的意象。

latinIntro.en: Latin cavus and cavare give cavity, cave, excavate and excavation; ex- supplies the outward direction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cavus 与 cavare 衍生 cavity、cave、excavate 与 excavation；ex- 提供向外方向。

items.example: The prefix makes the hollowing an outward removal.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀使挖空成为向外的移走。

items.example: The root supplies the shape of the result.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供结果的形状。

items.example: Latin used it for both earth and buried things.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语用它兼指泥土与埋藏物。

items.meaning: to remove material to expose or hollow
items.meaningCN: 移走材料以暴露或挖空
items.example: They excavated the pit in squares.
items.exampleCN: 他们把坑划成方格挖掘。

items.meaning: the act or result of digging
items.exampleCN: 这次发掘用了三个季度。

items.meaning: one who or that which digs
items.example: The excavator reached the clay layer.
The cavity was cleaned before filling.

latinEntries.structure: cavus, cava, cavum (adj., first and second declension)

definition_zh: 发掘；考古发掘工作、现场或成果；土方开挖；挖出的坑
definition_en: the process of digging out earth or buried material, especially for archaeology, or the hole made by digging
core_image: 方形探坑一层层向下收窄，坑壁插着标签，坑底露出石砌地面
scene: 工地被划成整齐的方格，工人用小铲一层层刮去表土，坑壁贴上编号纸条，坑底渐渐露出石砌地面。The excavation, the careful digging of a buried site, uncovered a wall that had lain under the field for centuries.
sceneCN: 这里 excavation 指「考古发掘的过程与工程」（第 1 个义项：有方法地把埋藏物挖出并记录）；句意为这次发掘揭开了一道在田野下埋了数百年的墙。可辨识物件：方格探坑、小铲、编号纸条、石砌地面、土堆。

pos.zh: 发掘；开挖；发掘现场或坑（可数，复数 excavations）

senses.title: The process of digging out buried material
senses.definition: the systematic removal of soil and deposits to expose remains or reach a level
senses.definitionCN: 有系统地移去土壤与堆积，以暴露遗存或到达某一层位
senses.example: The excavation uncovered a wall that had lain under the field for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这次发掘揭开了一道在田野下埋了数百年的墙。
senses.why: ex- 'out' plus cavare 'to hollow' gives 'hollow out'; the noun names the whole act of making a hollow.
senses.whyCN: ex-「出」加 cavare「挖空」构成「挖出空洞」；名词指整个挖空行为。

senses.title: The site or pit of a dig
senses.definition: the place, trench or pit where digging is under way
senses.definitionCN: 正在挖掘的地点、探沟或坑
senses.example: Visitors were kept back from the excavation.
senses.exampleCN: 参观者被挡住，不能靠近发掘现场。
senses.why: the act and the place share one word because the hole is the act's visible result.
senses.whyCN: 行为与地点共用一个词，因为坑就是行为可见的结果。

senses.title: The finds produced by a dig
senses.definition: the objects and records recovered in the course of digging
senses.definitionCN: 挖掘过程中获得的物件与记录
senses.example: The excavation produced three coins and a seal.
senses.exampleCN: 这次发掘出三枚硬币和一枚印章。
senses.why: a dig is judged by what it yields, so the noun can stand for its output.
senses.whyCN: 一次发掘以其收获来评判，因此名词可代指其产出。

senses.title: Earthwork or engineering cut
senses.definition: the removal of soil for a foundation, road, tunnel or canal
senses.definitionCN: 为地基、道路、隧道或运河而移走土壤
senses.example: The excavation for the tunnel took two years.
senses.exampleCN: 隧道开挖花了两年。
senses.why: the engineering sense came first in English; archaeology later borrowed the same term.
senses.whyCN: 英语中工程义先出现，考古学后来借用了同一术语。

senses.title: The archaeological method
senses.definition: the controlled technique of digging in layers, recording context and preserving finds
senses.definitionCN: 按层位挖掘、记录背景并保存器物的受控技术
senses.example: Modern excavation records every layer before removing it.
senses.exampleCN: 现代发掘在移除每一层之前先作记录。
senses.why: once digging became a science, the word named a method rather than mere earth-moving.
senses.whyCN: 当挖掘成为科学，这个词就命名方法，而不只是搬土。

senses.title: The hole or trench left behind
senses.definition: the cavity, trench or cutting made by removal of material
senses.definitionCN: 因移走材料而形成的洞、沟或切口
senses.example: Rainwater collected in the old excavation.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水积在旧坑里。
senses.why: the result persists after the work ends, and the noun covers that persistent shape.
senses.whyCN: 工作结束后结果仍在，名词也涵盖这一持久形状。

senses.title: Metaphor: deep investigation
senses.definition: by extension, a thorough inquiry that removes layers of concealment
senses.definitionCN: 引申指层层去除掩盖的彻底调查
senses.example: The journalist's excavation of the files took months.
senses.exampleCN: 记者对这些档案的「发掘」花了数月。
senses.why: the metaphor treats secrecy as soil: each layer removed brings evidence closer.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把秘密当作泥土：每移走一层，证据就更近一步。

senses.title: Abstraction: the uncovering of what was buried
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：把埋藏之物揭开
senses.definition: any process by which something covered or forgotten is brought into view
senses.definitionCN: 任何使被覆盖或被遗忘之物显现的过程
senses.example: Excavation is memory done with tools.
senses.exampleCN: 发掘是用工具进行的记忆。
senses.why: the deepest sense is revelation by removal, whether the layers are earth, paper or silence.
senses.whyCN: 最深的一层是「移除以显现」，无论层是泥土、纸张还是沉默。

intro.en: Excavation comes from Latin excavare, ex- 'out' plus cavare 'to make hollow', from cavus 'hollow'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: excavation 来自拉丁 excavare，由 ex-「出」与 cavare「挖空」构成，后者源于 cavus「空的」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cavus meant 'hollow, excavated'; it also gave English cavity and cave through related forms.
items.cn: cavus 意为「空的、挖空的」；它也经相关形式衍生英语 cavity 与 cave。

items.en: Cavare meant 'to make hollow, to dig out'; it turned the adjective into a verb of action.
items.cn: cavare 意为「使成空、挖出」；它把形容词变成动作动词。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus cavare produced excavare, 'to hollow out, dig out'.
items.cn: ex-「出」加 cavare 构成 excavare，意为「挖空、挖出」。

items.en: Excavatio named a hollowing out; English excavation came from this action noun.
items.cn: excavatio 指挖空；英语 excavation 来自这个行为名词。

items.en: Excavation entered English in the seventeenth century for earthworks; the archaeological sense developed in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: excavation 在十七世纪进入英语，指土方工程；考古义在十九世纪发展起来。

items.en: Source uncertain (first English date and root shape): dictionaries differ on the earliest English use, and the pre-Latin root of cavus is reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（英语首见年代与词根形态）：辞书对最早的英语用例说法不一，cavus 的拉丁语前词根属重构。

note.en: Group one holds digging words easily confused with excavation; group two holds neighbouring ideas of removal and discovery.
note.cn: 第一组是易与 excavation 混淆的挖掘类词；第二组是移走与发现的邻近概念。

entries.definition: To carry out excavation; the noun names the work, the verb names the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 指进行发掘；名词指工作，动词指去做。

entries.definition: A person or machine that excavates; it names the doer, not the deed.
entries.definitionCN: 指实施开挖的人或机器；命名施动者，而非行为。

entries.definition: A hollow space, especially in a tooth or body; it shares the root but names the void, not the work.
entries.definitionCN: 指空洞，尤指牙体或身体中的腔；同词根，但命名空处，而非工作。

entries.definition: A long narrow ditch; it can be the product of excavation or a separate military work.
entries.definitionCN: 指狭长沟；它可以是开挖的产物，也可以是单独的军事工事。

entries.definition: To break and remove ground; it is general and informal, while excavation implies method and record.
entries.definitionCN: 指破土并移走土；日常而宽泛，而 excavation 暗示方法与记录。

entries.definition: Digging to extract ore or coal; its purpose is economic, not archaeological.
entries.definitionCN: 指为开采矿石或煤而挖；目的在经济效益，而非考古。

entries.definition: Taking stone or sand from an open pit; the scale and purpose differ from a research dig.
entries.definitionCN: 指从露天坑取石或取砂；规模与目的不同于研究性发掘。

entries.definition: Bringing a buried thing to light; it stresses the find rather than the whole process.
entries.definitionCN: 指使埋藏物见光；强调发现，而非整个过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin pieces, the engineering-first history and the layer-by-layer method.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁成分、工程义在先的历史，以及逐层发掘的方法。

normal.en: ex- 'out' + cavare 'hollow': to hollow out the ground.
normal.cn: ex-「出」+ cavare「挖空」：把地面挖空。

normal.en: The family runs excavate, excavation, excavator, cavity, cave.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 excavate、excavation、excavator、cavity、cave。

normal.en: Engineering came first in English; archaeology borrowed the word later.
normal.cn: 英语中工程义在先；考古学后来借用了这个词。

normal.en: A modern dig records each layer before removing it.
normal.cn: 现代发掘在移除每一层之前先记录。

normal.en: Typical partners are archaeological, rescue, site and work.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是「考古的」「抢救性的」「现场」与「工程」。

abstract.en: Picture a hole that is also a notebook: every spadeful is written down.
abstract.cn: 想象一个坑同时也是一本笔记：每一铲都被记下。

abstract.en: Picture layers of paint removed from a wall until an older image appears.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上的层层颜料被去掉，直到旧画显现。

abstract.en: Picture a secret buried in paper rather than soil.
abstract.cn: 想象一个秘密埋在纸里，而不是土里。

examples.en: The excavation was halted when the water table rose.
examples.cn: 当地下水位上升时，发掘被停止。

examples.en: Every excavation destroys what it does not record.
examples.cn: 每一次发掘都会毁掉它未记录的东西。

examples.en: The road excavation exposed three old foundations.
examples.cn: 道路开挖露出了三处旧地基。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）+ cav（洞）+ ation」——把洞挖出来 → 发掘；开挖

root: 拉丁 excavatio，来自 excavare「挖空」= ex-（出）+ cavare（使空），cavare 源于 cavus「空的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one hollow: earth is removed. The hollow becomes a process, a place, a set of finds, an engineering cut, a method, a lasting hole, a metaphor for inquiry and finally any uncovering by removal.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个空洞展开：土被移走。这个空洞先成为过程，再成为地点、一组出土物、工程切口、方法、留下的坑、调查的比喻，最后成为任何「移除以显现」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stepped pit narrowing downward, tags on the walls, a stone floor at the bottom.
core.cn: 核心意象：逐层收窄的阶梯探坑，坑壁插着标签，坑底露出石地面。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE PLACE: the hollow is both work and workplace.
branches.cn: 行为与地点：空洞既是工作，也是工作场所。

branches.en: THE YIELD AND THE HOLE: what comes out and what remains are two ends of one act.
branches.cn: 收获与坑：取出之物与留下之物是同一行为的两端。

branches.en: ENGINEERING AND METHOD: moving soil becomes a science when records matter.
branches.cn: 工程与方法：当记录变得重要，搬土就成为科学。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: secrecy is soil, and inquiry is the spade.
branches.cn: 比喻：秘密是土，调查是铲。

branches.en: REVELATION BY REMOVAL: the deepest sense covers earth, paper and silence alike.
branches.cn: 移除以显现：最深的一层同时涵盖泥土、纸张与沉默。

intro.en: Excavation is a Latin verb plus an action suffix; the root cavus also builds words for hollow spaces.
intro.cn: excavation 是拉丁动词加行为后缀；词根 cavus 也构成表示空腔的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin cavus and cavare give cavity, cave, excavate and excavation; ex- adds the direction outward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cavus 与 cavare 衍生 cavity、cave、excavate 与 excavation；ex- 增添向外的方向。

items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出向外的移走。

items.example: The adjective describes the space made.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述被造出的空间。

items.example: The verb turns emptiness into an action.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把「空」变成动作。

items.example: The Latin verb covered both engineering and burial.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词兼指工程与埋藏。

items.example: Excavation names the process and its result.
They excavated the floor to the bedrock.

items.structure: excavate + -or (one who or that which acts)
items.example: The excavator lifted a bucket of clay.
The cavity in the tooth was filled.
The cave kept a constant temperature.

latinEntries.structure: cavus, cava, cavum (adj., first and second declension)

definition_en: to be greater than a limit or to do better than others
core_image: 赛跑选手冲线时越过计分板上的旧纪录
scene: 马拉松终点前，一名选手越过了赛会保持多年的纪录。Her time exceeded the old record by two seconds.
sceneCN: 这里 exceed 是「超过」（第 1 个义项：在数量或程度上大于）；句意：马拉松终点前，一名选手越过了赛会保持多年的纪录。

senses.title: Being greater
senses.definition: to be more than a number or limit
senses.definitionCN: 在数量上大于某个数字或限度
senses.example: The cost exceeded our budget.
senses.exampleCN: 费用超出了我们的预算。
senses.why: The verb marks a step past a fixed line.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词标记跨过一条固定的线。

senses.title: Going beyond
senses.definition: to go past what is allowed
senses.definitionCN: 越过被允许的界限
senses.example: He was fined for exceeding the speed limit.
senses.exampleCN: 他因超速被罚款。
senses.why: Crossing a limit is the same step, now against rules.
senses.whyCN: 越界是同一个动作，只是这次触犯了规则。

senses.title: Doing better
senses.definition: to do better than someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 表现得比某人或某物更好
senses.example: She exceeded all her rivals in the final round.
senses.exampleCN: 她在最后一轮中胜过了所有对手。
senses.why: Outrunning others is exceeding them.
senses.whyCN: 跑在别人前面就是胜过他们。

intro.en: Exceed comes from Latin excedere, to go out or go beyond.
intro.cn: exceed 源自拉丁语 excedere，意为走出、越过。

items.en: Cedere means to go or yield.
items.cn: cedere 意为走或让出。

items.en: Excedere joins ex-, out, with cedere, to go.
items.cn: excedere 由 ex-（出）与 cedere（走）组成。

items.en: Old French exceder keeps the sense of going beyond.
items.cn: 古法语 exceder 保留了越过的含义。

items.en: English exceed means to pass a limit.
items.cn: 英语 exceed 意为越过限度。

items.en: It now covers numbers, limits and rivals.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖数字、限度与对手。

note.en: Exceed is the verb; excess is the noun for too much.
note.cn: exceed 是动词，excess 是表示「过量」的名词。

entries.definition: an amount that is too much
to be better or greater than

normalIntro.en: To exceed is to step out past a line.
normalIntro.cn: exceed 就是跨出界线一步。

normal.en: Excess is the noun from exceed.
normal.cn: excess 是 exceed 对应的名词。

normal.en: Excessive means far too much.
normal.cn: excessive 意为过多。

normal.en: To exceed the limit is to cross it.
normal.cn: exceed the limit 就是越过界限。

normal.en: Sales exceeded expectations last year.
normal.cn: 去年销售额超出预期。

normal.en: Exceed and excess share the same root.
normal.cn: exceed 与 excess 同根。

abstract.en: Picture a runner's foot landing past the line.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者的脚落在终点线之外。

abstract.en: Imagine a glass filled beyond its rim.
abstract.cn: 想象杯子被倒得溢过杯口。

abstract.en: Think of an arrow flying past the target.
abstract.cn: 想象一支箭飞过靶子。

examples.en: The bill exceeded what we had planned.
examples.cn: 账单超出了我们的计划。

examples.en: Demand for the tickets far exceeded supply.
examples.cn: 门票需求远远超过供给。

examples.en: He exceeded the speed limit on the highway.
examples.cn: 他在高速公路上超速了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）＋ ceed（走）」——走出界限，就是超过。

root: 拉丁语 excedere（走出）＝ ex-（出）＋ cedere（走）→ 古法语 exceder → exceed，核心义「走出既定的界线」。

sensesIntro.en: Exceed means to be greater than a number, to pass an allowed limit, or to do better than others.
sensesIntro.cn: exceed 意为在数量上更大、越过允许的界限或胜过他人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot landing beyond the finish line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚落在终点线之外。

branches.en: Stepping past the line makes a number too large.
branches.cn: 跨过界线使数字变得过大。

branches.en: The same step breaks an allowed limit.
branches.cn: 同一个动作越过了允许的限度。

branches.en: Outrunning a rival is also exceeding.
branches.cn: 跑在对手前面也是 exceed。

branches.en: Numbers and rules both draw lines to pass.
branches.cn: 数字与规则都划出可被越过的线。

branches.en: Being greater and doing better share one image.
branches.cn: 数量更大与表现更好共用同一个意象。

intro.en: Exceed combines ex-, out, with Latin cedere, to go.
intro.cn: exceed 由 ex-（出）与拉丁语 cedere（走）组成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb excedere, to go out, passes through French into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 excedere（走出）经法语进入英语。

items.exampleCN: cedere 出现在 proceed 中。

items.example: Cede is the short English form.
items.exampleCN: cede 是简短的英语形式。

items.example: Exceed keeps the sense of stepping out.
items.exampleCN: exceed 保留了走出的含义。

items.example: Excess names the result of passing.
items.exampleCN: excess 指越过后产生的结果。

items.example: Proceed shares the same cedere root.
items.exampleCN: proceed 共享同一个 cedere 词根。

latinEntries.exampleCN: cedere 是 proceed 与 exceed 的基础。

latinEntries.example: Excedere is the source of exceed.
latinEntries.exampleCN: excedere 是 exceed 的来源。

definition_zh: 卓越；优秀；长处；杰出表现
definition_en: the quality of being extremely good, or a particular way of being very good
core_image: 一座高出周围屋顶的塔尖，从一片屋檐之上露出来
scene: 毕业典礼上，校长把奖章挂到那个连续三年拿下数学竞赛冠军的学生胸前。Her excellence in mathematics won her a scholarship to a top university.
sceneCN: 这里 excellence 是「卓越、杰出」（第 1 个义项：极高的水准）；句意：她在数学上的卓越表现为她赢得了顶尖大学的奖学金。

pos.zh: 卓越；优秀；长处；杰出表现

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词词尾 -ence 得到的动词，义为「出类拔萃；擅长」
拉丁语现在分词转成的形容词，义为「极好的；优秀的」
形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「极好地」

senses.title: The quality of being extremely good
senses.definition: a very high standard of quality or ability that stands out from the ordinary
senses.definitionCN: 远超一般水平的质量或能力
senses.example: The school is known for the excellence of its teaching.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校以卓越的教学质量著称。
senses.why: Latin excellere means to rise above, so excellence is literally the state of standing higher than the rest.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 excellere 意为「高出、超越」，所以 excellence 字面上就是「站得比其余的都高」的状态。

senses.title: A particular strength
senses.definition: one specific quality in which a person or thing is very good
senses.definitionCN: 人或事物在某一方面特别出色的具体优点
senses.example: His chief excellence as a teacher is patience.
senses.exampleCN: 作为教师，他最大的长处是耐心。
senses.why: Once the quality can be counted, the abstract noun names one item on a list of strengths, which is how the plural excellences works.
senses.whyCN: 当这种品质可以被数出来时，抽象名词就指长处清单上的一项，复数 excellences 正是这样用的。

senses.title: Outstanding performance in a field
senses.definition: a level of achievement that stands out in a subject, a sport, or a profession
senses.definitionCN: 在学科、运动或职业中脱颖而出的成就水平
senses.example: The prize rewards excellence in scientific research.
senses.exampleCN: 该奖项奖励在科学研究中的杰出表现。
senses.why: The preposition in ties the noun to a field, so excellence becomes a measurable standing inside that field rather than general praise.
senses.whyCN: 介词 in 把这个名词绑定到某个领域，于是 excellence 变成该领域内可衡量的水平，而不只是笼统的称赞。

senses.title: A recognized model of high quality
senses.definition: a place, group, or practice officially recognized as an outstanding example
senses.definitionCN: 被正式认定为杰出范例的地方、团体或做法
senses.example: The hospital was named a centre of excellence for heart surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院被评为心脏外科的卓越中心。
senses.why: Modern institutions turned the abstract quality into a title, so a building or a whole team can now carry the word as a name.
senses.whyCN: 现代机构把这种抽象品质变成了一个称号，于是一栋建筑或一整个团队如今可以把这个词当作名号来用。

intro.en: Excellence goes back to Latin excellere, to rise above, and reached English through Old French in the Middle Ages.
intro.cn: excellence 可追溯到拉丁语 excellere（高出、超越），中世纪经古法语进入英语。

items.en: The stem cellere means to rise or be high, seen also in celsus, lofty, and collis, hill.
items.cn: 词干 cellere 意为高起、处于高处，也见于 celsus（高耸的）与 collis（山丘）。

items.en: Excellere combines ex-, out, with cellere, and means to rise above or surpass.
items.cn: excellere 由 ex-（向外）与 cellere 组合，意为高出、超越。

items.en: Excellentia names superiority or pre-eminence in the classical period.
items.cn: 古典时期用 excellentia 表示优越、出众。

items.en: Old French takes the noun as excellence with the same meaning.
items.cn: 古法语以 excellence 的形式吸收这个名词，含义不变。

items.en: English records excellence in the fourteenth century as a word for superior quality.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪记下 excellence，指优越的品质。

items.en: Modern English adds fixed phrases such as centre of excellence and academic excellence.
items.cn: 现代英语又加上 centre of excellence 与 academic excellence 这类固定说法。

note.en: Excellence belongs to the same root as excel and excellent, and sits beside the nouns of merit and superiority.
note.cn: excellence 与 excel、excellent 同根，并与表示「优点、优越」的名词为邻。

entries.definition: to be very good at something
a title of honour for high officials
entries.definitionCN: 对高级官员的尊称「阁下」

entries.definition: a good quality that deserves praise
the state of being better than others
excellence shown in work or results

normalIntro.en: Excellence and excel share one Latin verb for rising above, so the noun is a height rather than a score.
normalIntro.cn: excellence 与 excel 共享同一个表示「高出」的拉丁动词，所以这个名词是高度，而不是分数。

normal.en: The verb behind the noun is excel, to rise above others.
normal.cn: 名词背后的动词是 excel，意为高出他人。

normal.en: The adjective excellent keeps the same idea of standing out.
normal.cn: 形容词 excellent 保留了同样的突出意味。

normal.en: Excellence in a subject names the field after the preposition in.
normal.cn: excellence in 后面的介词 in 点出的是哪个领域。

normal.en: A centre of excellence is an institution that carries the word as a title.
normal.cn: a centre of excellence 是把这个词当作名号的机构。

normal.en: Compare superiority: superiority compares two things, excellence praises the standard itself.
normal.cn: 对比 superiority：superiority 比较两样东西，excellence 则直接称赞水准本身。

abstract.en: Picture one tower top rising above a row of roofs.
abstract.cn: 想象一座塔尖从一排屋顶之上冒出来。

abstract.en: Imagine a list of strengths with one entry written on each line.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长处清单，每一行写着一个条目。

abstract.en: Think of a scoreboard where one name sits far above the others.
abstract.cn: 想象一块记分牌，有一个名字远远排在别人上面。

examples.en: The judges praised the excellence of the design.
examples.cn: 评委称赞这项设计的卓越。

examples.en: She won a national award for excellence in teaching.
examples.cn: 她获得了表彰卓越教学的国家奖。

examples.en: No one doubts his excellence as a pianist.
examples.cn: 没有人怀疑他作为钢琴家的卓越水平。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一颗赛伦斯」——赛场上最亮的那「一颗」星，水平超出同辈之上；拆开看是 ex 加 cellere（高起），这才是词源线索，谐音只是辅助联想。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外、超出）+ cellere（高起、隆起）→ excellere（高出、超越）→ excellentia（优越）→ 古法语 excellence → 英语 excellence，核心义「高出众人之上」。

sensesIntro.en: Excellence begins as a high standard, then a countable strength, then outstanding work in one field, and finally an institution honoured with the word.
sensesIntro.cn: excellence 先指很高的水准，再指可数的一项长处，然后指某个领域里的杰出表现，最后指被授予这个词的机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tower top standing above the surrounding roofs.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座塔尖高过四周的屋顶。

branches.en: Standing higher than the rest is the core sense of high quality.
branches.cn: 站得比别人高，就是「高品质」这一核心义。

branches.en: The same height can be counted one peak at a time, giving a strength.
branches.cn: 同样的高度可以一座峰一座峰地数，于是有了一项长处。

branches.en: Set inside a field, the height becomes a measurable achievement.
branches.cn: 把它放进某个领域，这个高度就变成可衡量的成就。

branches.en: Institutions borrowed the word as a title, so the quality became a name.
branches.cn: 机构把这个词借来当称号，于是品质变成了名号。

branches.en: Both the general standard and the field-specific award rest on the same upward image.
branches.cn: 笼统的水准与特定领域的奖项，都建立在同一个「向上」的意象上。

intro.en: Excellence grows from the Latin verb excellere, with English excel, excellent, and excellently built on the same stem.
intro.cn: excellence 从拉丁语动词 excellere 长出，英语的 excel、excellent 与 excellently 都建在同一词干上。

latinIntro.en: Latin excellere means to rise above, formed from ex-, out, and cellere, to rise or be high.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 excellere 意为高出、超越，由 ex-（向外）与 cellere（高起）构成。

items.example: The prefix ex- marks the movement upward and beyond.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 标出向上、超出的方向。

items.example: Cellere supplies the image of height.
items.exampleCN: cellere 提供「高度」这一意象。

items.example: Celsus shows the same high root as a adjective.
items.exampleCN: celsus 以形容词形式显示同一个「高」的词根。

items.example: Excellere is the direct source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: excellere 是整个词族的直接来源。

items.example: Excellentia carries the noun sense into French.
items.exampleCN: excellentia 把名词义带入法语。

items.example: The suffix -ence turns the stem into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ence 把词干变成状态名词。

items.example: Excellence keeps the abstract sense of the Latin noun.
items.exampleCN: excellence 保留拉丁名词的抽象含义。

items.example: Excel is the short English verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: excel 是这个词族里简短的英语动词。

items.example: Excellent describes the thing that stands above others.
items.exampleCN: excellent 描述高出其他事物的人或物。

definition_en: extremely good in quality or performance
core_image: 舞台上赢得全场掌声的表演者
scene: 她在比赛中表现非常出色，赢得全场掌声。Her performance in the contest was excellent and won loud applause.
sceneCN: 这里 excellent 是「出色的」（第 1 个义项：质量或表现极佳）；句意：她在比赛中表现非常出色，赢得全场掌声。

senses.title: Of the best quality
senses.definition: extremely good in quality
senses.definitionCN: 质量上极其出色
senses.example: The hotel serves excellent food.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店提供极好的食物。
senses.why: Something excellent rises above the ordinary.
senses.whyCN: excellent 的东西高出一般水平。

senses.title: Very well done
senses.definition: showing very high ability in an activity
senses.definitionCN: 在某项活动中展现很高能力

root: 拉丁语 excellere（高出）＝ ex-（出）＋ cellere（高耸）→ excellent，核心义「高出一般、超越众人」。

definition_zh: 除…之外；除了；把…排除在外
definition_en: not including someone or something, or to leave them out
core_image: 空着的那个座位
scene: 所有学生都去了博物馆，只有她留在教室。All the students went to the museum except her.
sceneCN: 这里 except 是「除…之外」（第 1 个义项：不包括某人）；句意：所有学生都去了博物馆，只有她留在教室。

senses.title: Not including
senses.definition: used to say that someone or something is not included
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示某人或某物不包括在内
senses.example: The shop opens daily except Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店除周日外每天开门。
senses.why: The word lifts one item out of the group.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把一项从群体中拿出来。

senses.title: Only that
senses.definition: used to add a single correction or condition
senses.definitionCN: 用于补充一个例外情况或条件

senses.why: One condition is taken out of the plan.

senses.title: To leave out

senses.exampleCN: 该规则把小额订单排除在外。
senses.why: The verb turns the exception into an act.
senses.whyCN: 动词把「例外」变成一种行为。

intro.en: Except comes from Latin excipere, to take out.
intro.cn: except 源自拉丁语 excipere，意为取出。

items.en: Capere means to take.

items.en: Excipere joins ex-, out, with capere, to take.

items.en: Old French excepter carries the sense of excluding.

items.en: English except marks the item left out.

items.en: Except for becomes a common phrase.

note.en: Except takes out one item; besides adds one more.

a short piece taken from a text

normalIntro.en: Except takes one item out of the group.

normal.en: Except for the rain, the day was fine.
normal.cn: except for 那场雨，这天很好。

normal.en: Everyone except Tom agreed.

normal.en: Except that adds one exception.

normal.en: Except when marks the only time.

normal.en: Present company excepted means you are not included.

root: 拉丁语 excipere（取出）＝ ex-（出）＋ capere（拿）→ except，核心义「把一项从整体中取出」。

sensesIntro.en: Except means not including, with one condition added, or to leave something out.

branches.en: The verb makes the exclusion deliberate.

branches.en: Item and condition both stand outside the rule.

branches.en: What is excepted is left out of the count.

intro.en: Except combines ex-, out, with Latin capere, to take.
intro.cn: except 由 ex-（出）与拉丁语 capere（拿）组成。

latinIntro.en: Excipere gives French excepter and then English except.

sceneCN: 这里 exception 是「例外」（第 1 个义项：不遵循规则的个例）；句意：这条规则对每个人都适用，没有例外。

senses.title: A case outside the rule
senses.definition: a person or case not covered by a rule
senses.definitionCN: 不受某条规则约束的人或情况
senses.example: Everyone must pay, without exception.

senses.why: One case is taken out of the general rule.

senses.why: The phrase marks what has been left out.

senses.why: To object is to set your view outside the rest.

intro.en: Exception comes from Latin exceptio, a taking out or a special case.
intro.cn: exception 源自拉丁语 exceptio，意为取出或特例。

items.en: Excipere means to take out.
items.cn: excipere 意为取出。

items.en: Exceptio is the act of taking out.

items.en: French exception names a special case.
items.cn: 法语 exception 指特例。

items.en: English exception keeps the legal flavour.
items.cn: 英语 exception 保留了法律色彩。

items.en: Take exception means object.

note.en: An exception leaves the rule; an anomaly is a strange case itself.
note.cn: exception 是规则之外的个例，anomaly 是本身反常的现象。

entries.definition: something that differs from the norm

normalIntro.en: An exception is a case held outside the rule.
normalIntro.cn: exception 是被留在规则之外的情况。

normal.en: To make an exception is to allow one special case.
normal.cn: make an exception 就是允许一个特例。

normal.en: With the exception of means except.

normal.en: No exception means the rule is firm.

normal.en: Take exception to means object to.

normal.en: An exception proves the rule.

abstract.en: Picture one red door in a white wall.
abstract.cn: 想象白墙上的一扇红门。

abstract.en: Imagine one footnote under a long page.
abstract.cn: 想象长页下方的一条脚注。

abstract.en: Think of one stone left on the wrong bank.
abstract.cn: 想象一块被遗在错误岸边的石头。

examples.en: This is an exception to the usual rule.
examples.cn: 这是通常规则的一个例外。

examples.en: They made an exception for her age.
examples.cn: 他们因为她的年龄破了例。

examples.en: He took exception to the unfair remark.
examples.cn: 他对那句不公平的话表示异议。

root: 拉丁语 exceptio（取出）→ 古法语 exception → exception，核心义「被从通则中取出的特例」。

sensesIntro.en: An exception is a case outside a rule, the act of leaving something out, or an objection.
sensesIntro.cn: exception 指规则之外的个例、排除在外的行为，或异议。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one case standing outside a rule.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在规则之外的个例。

branches.en: The special case is the main sense.
branches.cn: 特例是主要义项。

branches.en: Leaving something out is the act.
branches.cn: 排除在外是一种行为。

branches.en: Objection sets one voice outside the rest.
branches.cn: 异议让一个声音站到其余之外。

branches.en: A special case is what has been left out.
branches.cn: 特例就是被排除在外的那个。

branches.en: Exclusion and objection both divide a group.
branches.cn: 排除与异议都在划分群体。

intro.en: Exception is except plus the noun suffix -ion.
intro.cn: exception 是 except 加名词后缀 -ion。

latinIntro.en: Latin exceptio comes from excipere, to take out.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 exceptio 来自 excipere（取出）。

latinEntries.example: Exceptio is the root of exception.
