definition_zh: 杰出的；非凡的；异常的；例外的
definition_en: unusually good, or unusually different from the normal case
core_image: 一排同样高的树里，有一棵高出许多，树梢几乎碰到云。
scene: 音乐老师听完所有学生的演奏。After hearing every student play, the music teacher says only that this child's pitch is exceptional.
sceneCN: 这里 exceptional 是「远高于一般水平的、杰出的」（第 1 个义项：异常优秀或令人印象深刻）；句意：听完所有学生演奏后，音乐老师只说这个孩子的音准极为出色。

pos.zh: 杰出的；非凡的；异常的；例外的；特殊教育的

senses.title: Far above average
senses.titleCN: 杰出的：远高于一般水平
senses.definition: unusually good or impressive, far above the average
senses.definitionCN: 异常优秀或令人印象深刻，远高于平均水平
senses.example: She has an exceptional ear for harmony.
senses.exampleCN: 她对和声有非凡的听觉。
senses.why: Exceptional starts from exception: the person is lifted out of the ordinary row. The direction of the lift here is upward.
senses.whyCN: exceptional 从‘例外’出发：这个人被从普通的一排里拎出来；这里的拎出方向是向上。

senses.title: Unusual or rare
senses.titleCN: 异常的：不常发生，因而显眼
senses.definition: unusual and therefore notable, without necessarily being good
senses.definitionCN: 不寻常因而值得注意，不一定含褒义
senses.example: The storm was exceptional for its early date.
senses.exampleCN: 这场风暴因来得太早而异常。
senses.why: Here the lift is sideways: the case simply does not sit in the usual distribution, and the judgement is neutral.
senses.whyCN: 这里的拎出是横向的：这一例干脆不在通常分布里，判断是中性的。

senses.title: Forming an exception
senses.definition: forming an exception to a rule or general statement
senses.definitionCN: 构成规则或一般陈述之外的特殊情形
senses.example: This is an exceptional case that the policy did not foresee.
senses.exampleCN: 这是政策没有预见到的例外情形。
senses.why: This is the literal legal sense: the adjective describes a case that has been taken out of the rule's scope.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面上的法律义：形容词描述一个被移出规则适用范围的情形。

senses.title: Outstanding student
senses.titleCN: 特别出色的学生：天赋或成绩超常
senses.definition: describing a pupil or student whose ability is far above the expected level
senses.definitionCN: 形容能力远高于预期水平的学生
senses.example: The school created a programme for exceptional learners.
senses.exampleCN: 学校为超常学习者设立了一个项目。
senses.why: Education uses the word as a neutral technical label for children at the far end of a distribution, whether that end is high or low.
senses.whyCN: 教育领域把这个词当作中性技术标签，指分布两端的孩子，既可以是高端，也可以是低端。

senses.title: Exceptional size or degree
senses.titleCN: 超常的：尺寸或强度超出常规
senses.definition: much larger, stronger, or more intense than is normal
senses.definitionCN: 比正常情况大得多、强得多或强烈得多
senses.example: The bridge was built to withstand exceptional loads.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥按承受超常荷载来建造。
senses.why: Engineering uses the word for values beyond the design range: the structure is designed for the ordinary and then checked for the exception.
senses.whyCN: 工程上用这个词指超出设计范围的数值：结构先按常规设计，再针对例外情形校核。

senses.title: Extraordinarily good quality
senses.definition: of extraordinarily high quality
senses.definitionCN: 质量高到少见的
senses.example: The wine was exceptional, even for that famous vineyard.
senses.exampleCN: 这款酒即使对那个著名酒庄而言也属卓越。
senses.why: The word praises by placing the object outside its class: it is not merely a good wine, it is a wine that leaves the category.
senses.whyCN: 这个词通过把对象放到同类之外来赞美：它不只是好酒，而是离开了‘好酒’这一类别。

senses.title: Special needs
senses.titleCN: 特殊教育的：需要额外支持的孩子
senses.definition: in education, describing children who need special support because of disability or high ability
senses.definitionCN: 教育中形容因残障或超常能力而需要额外支持的孩子
senses.example: Funding was increased for exceptional children in the district.
senses.exampleCN: 该学区增加了对特殊需求儿童的拨款。
senses.why: The euphemistic use keeps the logic of exception: these children fall outside the standard classroom design and need a separate arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 这个委婉用法保留例外逻辑：这些孩子落在标准课堂设计之外，需要单独安排。

senses.title: Exceptionally allowed
senses.titleCN: 破例允许的：作为特殊情况被批准
senses.definition: allowed only as a special case, contrary to the usual practice
senses.definitionCN: 仅作为特殊情况、违背通常做法而被允许
senses.example: The committee granted exceptional permission to use the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会破例批准使用礼堂。
senses.why: Here the adjective modifies the permission itself: the rule stays in place, but one case is allowed to step outside it.
senses.whyCN: 这里形容词修饰的是‘许可’本身：规则仍然有效，但有一个情形被允许跨到线外。

intro.en: Exceptional is exception plus -al. It first meant ‘forming an exception’; the sense ‘unusually good’ is a later 19c development.
intro.cn: exceptional 是 exception 加 -al。它最初意为“构成例外的”；“异常优秀”义是 19 世纪较晚的发展。

items.en: To take out, from ex- out and capere take. The participle exceptus supplies the stem seen in exception and exceptional.
items.cn: 取出，来自 ex-‘向外’与 capere‘拿’。分词 exceptus 提供了 exception 与 exceptional 中可见的词干。

items.en: A taking out, an exception. The noun entered English through French and kept a legal flavour for centuries.
items.cn: 取出、例外。该名词经法语进入英语，数百年间都带法律色彩。

items.en: Exceptional is recorded in the 17th century meaning ‘of the nature of an exception’. It described cases and conditions, not people's talents.
items.cn: exceptional 在 17 世纪有记录，意为‘属于例外性质的’。它描述情形与条件，不描述人的才能。

items.en: The sense ‘unusual, uncommon’ developed next. Anything rare enough to leave the ordinary class could be called exceptional.
items.cn: 接着发展出‘不寻常、罕见’义。任何罕见得足以离开普通类别的东西，都可称为 exceptional。

items.en: The positive sense ‘excellently unusual’ is recorded in the early 19c. Praise borrowed the logic of rarity: good beyond the normal range.
items.cn: 正面义‘异常优秀’在 19 世纪早期有记录。赞美借用了‘稀有’的逻辑：好到超出正常范围。

items.en: Special education fixed exceptional as a technical label in the 20c. Engineering and law kept the neutral ‘outside the normal range’ sense.
items.cn: 20 世纪特殊教育把 exceptional 固定为技术标签；工程与法律则保留中性的‘超出正常范围’义。

note.en: The first group shares the exception stem and includes two words that are often confused; the second compares adjectives of high quality or rarity.
note.cn: 第一组共享 exception 词干，并包含两个常被混淆的词；第二组比较表示‘高品质或罕见’的形容词。

entries.definition: a case outside a rule. Exceptional is the adjective describing such a case or a quality beyond the norm.
entries.definitionCN: 规则之外的案例；exceptional 是描述这类案例或超常性质的形容词。

entries.definition: open to objection; blameworthy. It is not a stronger form of exceptional and carries disapproval.
entries.definitionCN: 可反对的；该受批评的。它不是 exceptional 的比较级，而带不赞同意味。

entries.definition: beyond objection; entirely proper. It is the opposite of exceptionable, not of exceptional.
entries.definitionCN: 无可指摘的；完全妥当的。它是 exceptionable 的反义，不是 exceptional 的反义。

entries.definition: to an unusual degree. It often means ‘extremely’ rather than ‘as an exception’.
entries.definitionCN: 达到不寻常的程度；常表示‘极其’，而非‘作为例外地’。

entries.definition: exceptionally good, standing out from others. It is warmer and more evaluative than exceptional.
entries.definitionCN: 杰出、从众人中站出来的；比 exceptional 更温暖、更具评价性。

entries.definition: very unusual or remarkable. It stresses departure from the ordinary order rather than from a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 非常不寻常或非凡；强调离开‘寻常秩序’，而非离开某条规则。

entries.definition: not happening often. It is neutral and can describe bad as easily as good.
entries.definitionCN: 不常发生的；中性，可描述坏也可描述好。

entries.definition: existing in small numbers or occurring seldom. It is about frequency, not quality.
entries.definitionCN: 数量少或很少发生；讲频率，不讲质量。

entries.definition: deviating from what is standard or expected. It sounds technical and often implies a problem.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离标准或预期的；听起来技术化，常暗示有问题。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: exception plus -al. The person or thing is lifted out of the ordinary row, either upward or sideways.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：exception 加 -al。人或物被从普通的一排里拎出来，方向可上可侧。

normal.en: Exception plus -al: exceptional means standing outside the ordinary row.
normal.cn: exception 加 -al：exceptional 就是站在普通队列之外。

normal.en: The tallest tree in a row is exceptional without breaking any rule.
normal.cn: 一排树里最高的那棵，不违反任何规则，却就是 exceptional。

normal.en: Exceptional weather is not good weather; it is weather outside the normal range.
normal.cn: exceptional 天气不是好天气，而是正常范围之外的天气。

normal.en: An exceptional student is one the standard lesson plan cannot fully hold.
normal.cn: exceptional 学生，是标准教案装不下的那个学生。

normal.en: Exceptional permission keeps the rule and opens one door.
normal.cn: 破例许可保留规则，只打开一扇门。

abstract.en: Every scale creates exceptions at both ends; the word does not decide which end is good.
abstract.cn: 每个量表都在两端制造例外；这个词本身不决定哪一端是好的。

abstract.en: Praise and abnormality use the same grammar: outside the normal class.
abstract.cn: 赞美与异常用的是同一套语法：在正常类别之外。

abstract.en: What a society calls exceptional is a map of what it expects.
abstract.cn: 一个社会称为 exceptional 的东西，就是它期待的分布图。

examples.en: The orchestra gave an exceptional performance despite the broken string.
examples.cn: 尽管琴弦断了，乐团仍奉献了一场非凡的演出。

examples.en: The judge allowed the evidence only under exceptional circumstances.
examples.cn: 法官仅在特殊情况下才允许采纳该证据。

examples.en: An exceptional year for rainfall left the reservoirs full.
examples.cn: 降雨异常充沛的一年让水库蓄满了水。

dict_mnemonic.text: “一颗赛破神”——一颗棋子破了神的常规，成了例外：exceptional 异常的、非凡的。

root: 由 exception 加 -al 构成，源头是拉丁 excipere（ex-‘向外’+ capere‘拿’）；本义为“属于例外性质的”，后引申出“罕见、异常优秀”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of exceptional, one move: lift a case out of the ordinary row. Upward lift gives ‘outstanding’, sideways lift gives ‘unusual’, legal lift gives ‘excepted’, and the classroom lift gives ‘special needs’.
sensesIntro.cn: exceptional 的八个义项共用一个动作：把一个情形从普通队列里拎出来。向上拎是‘杰出’，横向拎是‘异常’，法律拎是‘除外’，课堂拎是‘特殊需求’。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one tree in a row that rises far above the others.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排树中有一棵远远高出其他树。

branches.en: THE UPWARD LIFT: outstanding ability and exceptional quality leave the ordinary class from above.
branches.cn: 向上的拎出：非凡能力与卓越品质从上方离开普通类别。

branches.en: THE SIDEWAYS LIFT: rare weather and special permission simply sit outside the usual distribution.
branches.cn: 横向的拎出：异常天气与特殊许可只是位于通常分布之外。

branches.en: THE LEGAL LIFT: a case is formally removed from a rule's scope.
branches.cn: 法律上的拎出：情形被正式移出规则范围。

branches.en: THE EDUCATIONAL LIFT: pupils beyond the standard design, at either end, need a separate arrangement.
branches.cn: 教育上的拎出：超出标准设计的学童，无论高低端，都需要单独安排。

branches.en: THE ENGINEERING LIFT: loads beyond the design range are checked separately.
branches.cn: 工程上的拎出：超出设计范围的荷载被单独校核。

intro.en: Exceptional is exception plus the relational suffix -al. The adverb exceptionally often weakens into ‘extremely’, a sign of how far the word has travelled from law.
intro.cn: exceptional 是 exception 加关系后缀 -al。副词 exceptionally 常弱化为‘极其’，这说明该词离开法律有多远。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is capere, with the compound excipere and the noun exceptio. The same family yields accept, receive, and capture.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 capere，复合动词 excipere，名词 exceptio。同一词族还产生 accept、receive、capture。

items.example: The result was exceptional for its consistency.
items.exampleCN: 这个结果因一致性而异常出色。

items.example: The study examined exceptionality in early readers.
items.exampleCN: 该研究考察早期阅读者的超常现象。

items.meaning: the belief that a group is uniquely exempt from common rules
items.meaningCN: 例外论；认为某群体独特而不受共同规则约束的信念
items.example: The speech appealed to a sense of national exceptionalism.
items.exampleCN: 演讲诉诸一种民族例外论情感。

items.example: No one except the porter was allowed in.
items.exampleCN: 除搬运工外，任何人都不许进入。

items.example: The remark was exceptionable and was withdrawn.
items.exampleCN: 那句话可遭反对，因而被撤回。

items.example: He accepted the terms without complaint.
items.exampleCN: 他毫无怨言地接受了条件。

items.example: The sensor captured a faint signal.
items.exampleCN: 传感器捕捉到一个微弱信号。

definition_en: an amount that is too much, or more than is needed
core_image: 行李秤上超重的箱子
scene: 行李超过了规定重量，她只好为超出的部分付费。Her bag was over the limit, so she paid for the excess.
sceneCN: 这里 excess 是「超出部分」（第 2 个义项：超过限度的量）；句意：行李超过了规定重量，她只好为超出的部分付费。

senses.title: Too much of something
senses.definition: an amount that is more than is good or needed
senses.definitionCN: 超过适宜或所需的数量
senses.example: An excess of sugar is bad for teeth.
senses.exampleCN: 糖分过量对牙齿有害。
senses.why: The word names what spills past the right amount.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指溢出适宜量的部分。

senses.title: The amount over a limit
senses.definition: the amount by which something is over a limit
senses.definitionCN: 某物超过限度的数量
senses.example: You must pay for any excess.
senses.exampleCN: 超出的部分必须付费。
senses.why: A limit is crossed and the extra stays visible.
senses.whyCN: 越过限度后，多出的部分清晰可见。

senses.title: Extra in a bad way
senses.definition: more than is proper or allowed
senses.definitionCN: 超过适当或被允许的范围
senses.example: The airline charges for excess baggage.
senses.exampleCN: 航空公司对超重行李收费。
senses.why: The adjective marks luggage beyond the line.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标记超出界限的行李。

intro.en: Excess comes from Latin excessus, a going beyond, from excedere.
intro.cn: excess 源自拉丁语 excessus（越出），来自 excedere。

items.en: Excedere means to go beyond.
items.cn: excedere 意为越过。

items.en: Excessus is a going too far.
items.cn: excessus 意为走得过头。

items.en: French exces keeps the sense of overdoing.
items.cn: 法语 exces 保留过度之意。

items.en: English excess means too much or the extra part.
items.cn: 英语 excess 意为过多或超出部分。

items.en: In excess of becomes a formal phrase.
items.cn: in excess of 成为正式短语。

note.en: Excess is too much; surplus is simply what is left over.
note.cn: excess 指过多，surplus 指单纯剩余下来的部分。

entries.definition: an amount left after needs are met

normalIntro.en: Excess is what crosses the line and stays there.
normalIntro.cn: excess 就是越过界线后多出来的那部分。

normal.en: In excess of means more than.
normal.cn: in excess of 意为超过。

normal.en: Excess baggage costs extra at the airport.
normal.cn: excess baggage 在机场要额外付费。

normal.en: Eat to excess means eat far too much.
normal.cn: eat to excess 意为吃得过多。

normal.en: Excess weight is hard on the body.
normal.cn: excess weight 对身体负担很重。

normal.en: Excessive is the adjective from excess.
normal.cn: excessive 是 excess 的形容词。

abstract.en: Picture a cup spilling over its edge.
abstract.cn: 想象杯子从边缘溢出来。

abstract.en: Imagine a suitcase bulging past the scale.
abstract.cn: 想象行李箱鼓出秤面。

abstract.en: Think of a bill with one line too many.
abstract.cn: 想象账单上多出一行。

examples.en: There is an excess of oil in the pan.
examples.cn: 锅里油太多了。

examples.en: The fee is in excess of a hundred dollars.
examples.cn: 费用超过一百美元。

examples.en: He drank to excess at the party.
examples.cn: 他在聚会上喝得过量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）＋ cess（走）」——走出限度的那一部分，就是过量。

root: 拉丁语 excedere（越过）→ excessus（越出）→ excess，核心义「越过界线后多出来的部分」。

sensesIntro.en: Excess is too much of something, the amount over a limit, or an adjective for extra baggage.
sensesIntro.cn: excess 指某物过多、超过限度的部分，或作形容词表示超额的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup spilling over its edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：从杯沿溢出的水。

branches.en: Too much is the general sense.
branches.cn: 过多是整体义项。

branches.en: The extra over a limit is measurable.
branches.cn: 超过限度的部分是可计量的。

branches.en: The adjective labels what is over.
branches.cn: 形容词标记超出的东西。

branches.en: What is too much is exactly the extra.
branches.cn: 过多的东西正是多出来的部分。

branches.en: The extra amount becomes excess baggage.
branches.cn: 超出的量变成超重行李。

intro.en: Excess comes from Latin excedere, to go beyond.
intro.cn: excess 来自拉丁语 excedere（越过）。

latinIntro.en: Excessus, a going too far, is the direct source.
latinIntro.cn: excessus（走得过头）是直接来源。

items.exampleCN: excess 保留了多出的含义。

items.example: The phrase states a limit passed.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语表示越过的限度。

latinEntries.example: Excessus is the source of excess.
latinEntries.exampleCN: excessus 是 excess 的来源。

definition_en: much more than is reasonable or necessary
core_image: 音量开到极限的音响
scene: 邻居家的音乐声太大，已经超出了合理范围。The music from next door was excessive and far too loud.
sceneCN: 这里 excessive 是「过度的」（第 1 个义项：远远超过合理程度）；句意：邻居家的音乐声太大，已经超出了合理范围。

senses.title: More than reasonable
senses.definition: much more than is reasonable
senses.definitionCN: 远远超过合理程度
senses.example: The noise was excessive for a quiet street.
senses.exampleCN: 在安静的街道上，这噪音太过分了。
senses.why: The word judges an amount as beyond the line.
senses.whyCN: 这个词判定数量越过了界线。

senses.title: Beyond what is allowed
senses.definition: more than is allowed by rules or law
senses.definitionCN: 超过规则或法律允许的范围
senses.example: The guard used excessive force.
senses.exampleCN: 警卫使用了过度武力。
senses.why: A limit exists, and the act crossed it.
senses.whyCN: 界限存在，而行为越过了它。

senses.title: Too high in amount
senses.definition: unreasonably large in number or price
senses.definitionCN: 数量或价格高得不合理
senses.example: They charged an excessive price.
senses.exampleCN: 他们要价过高。
senses.why: A number past sense becomes excessive.
senses.whyCN: 超出常理的数字就是过高的。

intro.en: Excessive comes from Latin excessus, a going beyond.
intro.cn: excessive 源自拉丁语 excessus（越出）。

items.en: Excedere means to go beyond.
items.cn: excedere 意为越过。

items.en: Excessus is the act of going too far.
items.cn: excessus 是走得过头。

items.en: French excessif means overdone.
items.cn: 法语 excessif 意为过度。

items.en: English excessive judges amounts and acts.
items.cn: 英语 excessive 评判数量与行为。

items.en: It appears in law, health and prices.
items.cn: 它出现在法律、健康与价格领域。

note.en: Excessive is beyond reasonable; extreme is at the far end.
note.cn: excessive 指超出合理，extreme 指处于最远端。

normalIntro.en: Excessive means past the line of reason.
normalIntro.cn: excessive 意为越过了合理之线。

normal.en: Excessive noise disturbs a whole street.
normal.cn: excessive noise 会打扰整条街。

normal.en: Excessive force is never acceptable.
normal.cn: excessive force 绝不可接受。

normal.en: Excessive speed causes accidents.
normal.cn: excessive speed 会引发事故。

normal.en: Excessive drinking harms the body.
normal.cn: excessive drinking 伤害身体。

normal.en: The adverb form is excessively.
normal.cn: 副词形式是 excessively。

abstract.en: Picture a speaker turned past its limit.
abstract.cn: 想象音箱被调到超出极限。

abstract.en: Imagine a plate piled far too high.
abstract.cn: 想象盘子堆得过高。

abstract.en: Think of a price tag with one zero too many.
abstract.cn: 想象价签上多写了一个零。

examples.en: Excessive heat closed the schools.
examples.cn: 酷热使学校停课。

examples.en: The worker was punished for excessive delay.
examples.cn: 这名工人因过度拖延受到处罚。

examples.en: Excessive use of water harms the garden.
examples.cn: 过度浇水会伤害花园。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「excess（过量）＋ ive」——带着过量性质的，就是过度的。

root: 拉丁语 excessus（越出）＋ -ive → excessive，核心义「具有越界、过量性质的」。

sensesIntro.en: Excessive means far more than is reasonable, allowed, or sensible.
sensesIntro.cn: excessive 意为远远超过合理、允许或适度范围。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dial turned past its limit.
core.cn: 核心意象：旋钮被拧过极限。

branches.en: Beyond reason is the general sense.
branches.cn: 超出合理是整体义项。

branches.en: Beyond rules is the legal sense.
branches.cn: 超出规则是法律义项。

branches.en: Beyond a fair number is the price sense.
branches.cn: 超出公道数字是价格义项。

branches.en: Reason and law both draw a limit.
branches.cn: 常理与法律都画出界线。

branches.en: Force and price can both be pushed too far.
branches.cn: 武力与价格都可能被推得过远。

intro.en: Excessive is excess plus the adjective suffix -ive.
intro.cn: excessive 是 excess 加形容词后缀 -ive。

latinIntro.en: Excessus, a going beyond, lies behind the word.
latinIntro.cn: excessus（越出）是这个词背后的来源。

latinEntries.example: Excessus is the source of excessive.
latinEntries.exampleCN: excessus 是 excessive 的来源。

definition_en: to give something and receive something else in return
core_image: 车站里互相递出电话号码的两个人
scene: 两人在车站交换了电话号码。The two of them exchanged phone numbers at the station.
sceneCN: 这里 exchange 是「交换」（第 1 个义项：给出一样东西并换回另一样）；句意：两人在车站交换了电话号码。

senses.title: Swapping things
senses.definition: to give one thing and get another in return
senses.definitionCN: 给出一样东西并换回另一样
senses.example: They exchanged books after class.
senses.exampleCN: 课后他们交换了书。
senses.why: Each hand takes and gives at the same moment.
senses.whyCN: 每只手在同一时刻既拿又给。

senses.title: Changing money
senses.definition: to change money of one country for another
senses.definitionCN: 把一国货币换成另一国货币
senses.example: We exchanged dollars for local money.
senses.exampleCN: 我们把美元换成了当地货币。
senses.why: Currency is swapped like any other goods.
senses.whyCN: 货币像其他货物一样被互换。

senses.title: A talk or argument
senses.definition: a conversation or short argument between people
senses.definitionCN: 人与人之间的交谈或短暂争执
senses.example: They had a sharp exchange of words.
senses.exampleCN: 他们发生了激烈的口角。
senses.why: Words are handed back and forth like objects.
senses.whyCN: 话语像物品一样被来回递送。

intro.en: Exchange comes from Old French eschangier, from Latin cambiare, to barter.
intro.cn: exchange 源自古法语 eschangier，来自拉丁语 cambiare（以物易物）。

items.en: Cambiare means to barter or swap.
items.cn: cambiare 意为以物易物。

items.en: Eschangier adds the sense of giving in turn.
items.cn: eschangier 增加了轮流给予的含义。

items.en: Exchange enters English as a verb of swapping.
items.cn: exchange 以交换动词之意进入英语。

items.en: Currency exchange becomes a daily need.
items.cn: 货币兑换成为日常需求。

items.en: Exchange student names a school visitor.
items.cn: exchange student 指来校交流的学生。

note.en: Exchange is a two-way swap; change alone means make different.
note.cn: exchange 是双向互换，change 单指改变。

entries.definition: to exchange one thing for another
to buy and sell or swap

normalIntro.en: Exchange is a two-way hand-over.
normalIntro.cn: exchange 就是双向递交。

normal.en: The exchange rate tells what money is worth.
normal.cn: exchange rate 告诉我们货币的价值。

normal.en: Exchange ideas means share thoughts.
normal.cn: exchange ideas 意为分享想法。

normal.en: In exchange for means as a swap for.
normal.cn: in exchange for 意为作为…的交换。

normal.en: Foreign exchange deals with other currencies.
normal.cn: foreign exchange 涉及外币。

normal.en: An exchange student studies in another country.
normal.cn: exchange student 在另一个国家学习。

abstract.en: Picture two hands passing letters.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手互相递信。

abstract.en: Imagine two coins sliding across a counter.
abstract.cn: 想象两枚硬币在柜台上滑过。

abstract.en: Think of words flying back and forth.
abstract.cn: 想象话语来回飞舞。

examples.en: We exchanged gifts at the party.
examples.cn: 我们在聚会上交换了礼物。

examples.en: The bank exchanges foreign money.
examples.cn: 这家银行兑换外币。

examples.en: There was a short exchange of views.
examples.cn: 双方简短地交换了意见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）＋ change（换）」——把东西拿出来换，就是交换。

root: 拉丁语 cambiare（以物易物）→ 古法语 eschangier → exchange，核心义「双方互相给出并取得」。

sensesIntro.en: Exchange means to swap things, change currency, or have a talk or brief argument.
sensesIntro.cn: exchange 意为互换物品、兑换货币，或进行交谈与短暂争执。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands passing things.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手互相递交。

branches.en: Swapping objects is the core sense.
branches.cn: 交换物品是核心义项。

branches.en: Money is swapped on the same pattern.
branches.cn: 货币按同样模式互换。

branches.en: Words also travel in both directions.
branches.cn: 话语也双向流动。

branches.en: Goods and money both pass hand to hand.
branches.cn: 货物与钱都手手相传。

branches.en: A talk is an exchange of ideas.
branches.cn: 交谈就是想法的交换。

intro.en: Exchange joins ex-, out, with change.
intro.cn: exchange 由 ex-（出）与 change 组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin cambiare, to barter, is the older root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cambiare（以物易物）是更早的词根。

items.example: Exchangeable means able to be swapped.
The compound names a money price.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词指货币价格。
这个复合词指来访学生。

latinEntries.example: Cambiare is the old root of exchange.
latinEntries.exampleCN: cambiare 是 exchange 的古老词根。

definition_zh: 兴奋；激动；令人兴奋的事物
definition_en: a strong feeling of eager happiness or nervous energy
core_image: 音乐会开场前大厅里的低语
scene: 音乐会开始前，大厅里满是兴奋的低语。Before the concert, excitement filled the hall in low whispers.
sceneCN: 这里 excitement 是「兴奋」（第 1 个义项：强烈而期待的情绪）；句意：音乐会开始前，大厅里满是兴奋的低语。

pos.zh: 兴奋；激动；令人兴奋的事物

senses.title: Eager happiness
senses.definition: a happy feeling of looking forward to something
senses.definitionCN: 期待某事时的快乐感受
senses.example: Her eyes shone with excitement.
senses.exampleCN: 她兴奋得眼睛发亮。
senses.why: The feeling rises when something good is near.
senses.whyCN: 好事临近时这种感受就会升起。

senses.title: Nervous stir
senses.definition: a state of strong nervous energy
senses.definitionCN: 强烈而不安的情绪状态
senses.example: The crowd was in a state of excitement.
senses.exampleCN: 人群处于激动的状态。
senses.why: The same energy can be joy or nerves.
senses.whyCN: 同一种能量既可以是喜悦，也可以是紧张。

senses.title: An exciting thing
senses.definition: an event or activity that causes strong feeling
senses.definitionCN: 引起强烈感受的事件或活动
senses.example: The trip was full of excitement.
senses.exampleCN: 这次旅行充满令人兴奋的事。
senses.why: The feeling and the cause share one name.
senses.whyCN: 感受与原因共用一个名称。

intro.en: Excitement comes from exciter, the French verb from Latin excitare.
intro.cn: excitement 来自法语动词 exciter，其源头是拉丁语 excitare。

items.en: Excitare means to call out.
items.cn: excitare 意为唤出。

items.en: Exciter means to stir up.
items.cn: exciter 意为激起。

items.en: Excitement names the stirred state.
items.cn: excitement 指被激起的这种状态。

items.en: It covers both joy and nerves.
items.cn: 它同时涵盖喜悦与紧张。

items.en: The plural is rare but appears in travel writing.
items.cn: 复数形式少见，但会出现在游记中。

note.en: Excitement is the feeling; alarming is different; thrill is a stronger burst.
note.cn: excitement 是这种感受，thrill 是更强烈的爆发。

entries.definition: a sudden strong feeling of joy

normalIntro.en: Excitement is the inner spark before something begins.
normalIntro.cn: excitement 就是事情开始前心里的火花。

normal.en: In excitement means with a racing heart.
normal.cn: in excitement 意为心里怦怦跳地。

normal.en: Great excitement filled the room.
normal.cn: great excitement 充满了房间。

normal.en: Excitement about the trip kept them awake.
normal.cn: 对旅行的兴奋让他们睡不着。

normal.en: The news caused great excitement.
normal.cn: 这个消息引起了极大兴奋。

normal.en: The excitement of travel comes from the unknown.
normal.cn: the excitement of travel 来自未知。

abstract.en: Picture hands clapping before the lights go up.
abstract.cn: 想象灯光亮起前响起的掌声。

abstract.en: Imagine a child's first look at the sea.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子第一次看见大海。

abstract.en: Think of a crowd holding its breath.
abstract.cn: 想象人群屏住呼吸。

examples.en: The children could hardly hide their excitement.
examples.cn: 孩子们几乎藏不住兴奋。

examples.en: There was great excitement about the new bridge.
examples.cn: 人们为这座新桥兴奋不已。

examples.en: He spoke with excitement in his voice.
examples.cn: 他说话时声音里带着激动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「excite（使兴奋）＋ ment」——被唤起的状态，就是兴奋。

root: 拉丁语 excitare（唤出）→ 法语 exciter → excite ＋ -ment → excitement，核心义「被唤起并持续着的强烈情绪」。

sensesIntro.en: Excitement is eager happiness, nervous energy, or the event that stirs them.
sensesIntro.cn: excitement 是期待中的快乐、紧张的能量，或引起它们的事件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spark before the show begins.
core.cn: 核心意象：演出开始前的火花。

branches.en: Looking forward is the main feeling.
branches.cn: 期待是主要感受。

branches.en: The same energy can turn nervous.
branches.cn: 同样的能量也可能变紧张。

branches.en: The cause and the feeling share one word.
branches.cn: 原因与感受共用一个词。

branches.en: Joy and nerves both raise the pulse.
branches.cn: 喜悦与紧张都会让脉搏加快。

branches.en: A trip can both cause and be the excitement.
branches.cn: 旅行既能引起兴奋，也能就是那件令人兴奋的事。

intro.en: Excitement is excite plus the noun suffix -ment.
intro.cn: excitement 是 excite 加名词后缀 -ment。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb excitare is the deepest source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 excitare 是最深的来源。

items.example: -ment turns the verb into a noun.

latinEntries.example: Excitare is the source of excitement.
latinEntries.exampleCN: excitare 是 excitement 的来源。

definition_zh: 排除；不包括；把…拒之门外
definition_en: to keep someone or something out, or to leave them out
core_image: 名额已满后关上的门
scene: 因为名额有限，主办方不得不把一些申请者排除在外。Because places were limited, the organizers had to exclude some applicants.
sceneCN: 这里 exclude 是「把…排除在外」（第 1 个义项：不让某人进入或参与）；句意：因为名额有限，主办方不得不把一些申请者排除在外。

senses.title: Keeping someone out
senses.definition: to stop someone from entering or joining
senses.definitionCN: 阻止某人进入或加入
senses.example: The club excluded women for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这家俱乐部多年来排斥女性。
senses.why: The word closes a door on someone.
senses.whyCN: 这个词对某人关上了门。

senses.title: Not including
senses.definition: to leave something out of a group or list
senses.definitionCN: 把某物从群体或清单中略去
senses.example: The price excludes delivery.
senses.exampleCN: 价格不含送货费。
senses.why: One item is kept outside the count.
senses.whyCN: 一项被留在计数之外。

senses.title: Ruling out
senses.definition: to decide that something is not possible
senses.definitionCN: 断定某事不可能
senses.example: We cannot exclude the possibility of rain.
senses.exampleCN: 我们不能排除下雨的可能。
senses.why: A possibility is shut out of the answer.
senses.whyCN: 一种可能被关在答案之外。

intro.en: Exclude comes from Latin excludere, to shut out.
intro.cn: exclude 源自拉丁语 excludere，意为关在外面。

items.en: Claudere means to close or shut.
items.cn: claudere 意为关闭。

items.en: Excludere joins ex-, out, with claudere.
items.cn: excludere 由 ex-（出）与 claudere 组成。

items.en: French exclure keeps the sense of shutting out.
items.cn: 法语 exclure 保留关在外面之意。

items.en: English exclude covers people, items and ideas.
items.cn: 英语 exclude 涵盖人、物品与想法。

items.en: Excluding tax becomes a set phrase.
items.cn: excluding tax 成为固定短语。

note.en: Exclude is the opposite of include.
note.cn: exclude 是 include 的反义词。

normalIntro.en: To exclude is to close the door on someone.
normalIntro.cn: exclude 就是对某人关上门。

normal.en: Exclude from means keep out of a group.
normal.cn: exclude from 意为不让进入某个群体。

normal.en: Exclude the possibility means rule it out.
normal.cn: exclude the possibility 意为排除这种可能。

normal.en: The price excludes delivery.
normal.cn: 价格不含送货费。

normal.en: Excluding tax means before tax is added.
normal.cn: excluding tax 意为未加税前。

normal.en: Exclusion is the noun from exclude.
normal.cn: exclusion 是 exclude 的名词。

abstract.en: Picture a door closing in front of someone.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门在某人面前关上。

abstract.en: Imagine one name crossed off a list.
abstract.cn: 想象清单上一个名字被划掉。

abstract.en: Think of a gate locked after the last guest.
abstract.cn: 想象最后一位客人之后大门上锁。

examples.en: The list excludes names with no address.
examples.cn: 这份清单排除了没有地址的名字。

examples.en: Nobody should be excluded because of age.
examples.cn: 任何人都不应因年龄被排斥。

examples.en: We cannot exclude a later change.
examples.cn: 我们不能排除以后会有变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）＋ clude（关）」——关在门外，就是排除。

root: 拉丁语 excludere（关在外面）＝ ex-（出）＋ claudere（关闭）→ exclude，核心义「把人或事物关在范围之外」。

sensesIntro.en: Exclude means to keep someone out, leave something out, or rule out a possibility.
sensesIntro.cn: exclude 意为把某人拒之门外、不包括某物，或排除某种可能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door closed on someone.
core.cn: 核心意象：对某人关上的门。

branches.en: Keeping a person out is the main sense.
branches.cn: 把人挡在外面是主要义项。

branches.en: An item can be left out of a list.
branches.cn: 一项可以被从清单中略去。

branches.en: A possibility can be shut out of thought.
branches.cn: 一种可能可以被排除在考虑之外。

branches.en: People and items both stay outside.
branches.cn: 人与物品都被留在外面。

branches.en: Omitting a fact can rule out an option.
branches.cn: 略去一个事实可能排除一个选项。

intro.en: Exclude joins ex-, out, with Latin claudere, to close.
intro.cn: exclude 由 ex-（出）与拉丁语 claudere（关闭）组成。

latinIntro.en: Claudere also lies behind close and clause.
latinIntro.cn: claudere 也是 close 与 clause 的来源。

items.exampleCN: claudere 出现在 clause 中。
exclusive 意为把他人排除在外。

latinEntries.example: Excludere is the source of exclude.
latinEntries.exampleCN: excludere 是 exclude 的来源。

definition_zh: 排除；排斥；除外；被排除的状态；社会排斥
definition_en: the act of keeping someone or something out, or the state of being kept out
core_image: 一扇门在某人面前合上，门内是灯光和人群，门外只剩走廊。
scene: 实验室门口贴着「仅限授权人员」，新来的实习生被挡在门外。A sign on the lab door reads authorised staff only, and the new intern stands outside: that is exclusion.
sceneCN: 这里 exclusion 是「被排除在外、不得进入」（第 1 个义项：被挡在某个范围之外的状态）；句意：实验室门口贴着仅限授权人员，新来的实习生被挡在门外，这就是被排除在外。

pos.zh: 排除；排斥；除外；被排除状态；（生态）竞争排斥

senses.title: Shutting someone out
senses.definition: the act of preventing a person or thing from entering or taking part
senses.definitionCN: 阻止人或物进入或参与的行为
senses.example: The exclusion of non-members from the vote caused an outcry.
senses.exampleCN: 把非会员排除在投票之外引发了抗议。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to shut the door. Exclusion is that closing seen as an act: the boundary is drawn by whoever holds the door.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为‘关上门’。exclusion 就是这次关门被视为一个动作：边界由掌着门的人画出。

senses.title: The state of being left out
senses.titleCN: 被排除的状态：人在门外的那一侧
senses.definition: the condition of being left outside a group, place, or activity
senses.definitionCN: 被留在群体、场所或活动之外的状态
senses.example: Her exclusion from the committee lasted two years.
senses.exampleCN: 她被排除在委员会之外长达两年。
senses.why: The same event can be told from the door's other side. Here the noun names the experience of the one who remains outside.
senses.whyCN: 同一件事可以从门的另一侧讲述。这里的名词命名的是留在门外那个人的经历。

senses.title: Exclusion clause
senses.titleCN: 除外条款：合同里预先排除的责任
senses.definition: a contractual or insurance clause that removes a risk or item from cover
senses.definitionCN: 把某项风险或项目排除在保障之外的合同或保险条款
senses.example: The policy's exclusion for flood damage was printed in bold.
senses.exampleCN: 保单对洪水损害的除外责任用粗体印出。
senses.why: Contracts define the protected space first, then list what is shut out of it. The clause is the door drawn on paper.
senses.whyCN: 合同先划定受保护的空间，再列出被关在门外的项目。条款就是画在纸上的那扇门。

senses.title: Social exclusion
senses.titleCN: 社会排斥：被挡在正常生活之外
senses.definition: the process by which groups are pushed to the margins of society and denied normal participation
senses.definitionCN: 某些群体被推到社会边缘、无法正常参与的过程
senses.example: Poor transport links deepen the social exclusion of rural families.
senses.exampleCN: 交通不便加深了农村家庭的社会排斥。
senses.why: Here the door is not one building but a whole set of institutions: work, school, housing, and health. Exclusion becomes structural rather than personal.
senses.whyCN: 这里的门不是一栋楼，而是一整套制度：工作、学校、住房与医疗。排斥由此变成结构性的，而非个人性的。

senses.title: Competitive exclusion
senses.titleCN: 竞争排斥：两个物种不能长期占同一生态位
senses.definition: the ecological principle that two species competing for the same resource cannot coexist indefinitely
senses.definitionCN: 两个物种争夺同一资源时无法无限期共存的生态学原理
senses.example: Competitive exclusion drove the native species from the pond.
senses.exampleCN: 竞争排斥把本地物种逐出了池塘。
senses.why: One species uses the shared resource slightly better, so the other is gradually shut out of its own niche. The door here is closed by competition, not policy.
senses.whyCN: 一个物种对共享资源的利用略好，另一个就被逐渐关在自己的生态位之外。这里的门由竞争关上，而非政策。

senses.title: Tax exclusion
senses.titleCN: 不计入项：税法里不纳入收入的部分
senses.definition: an item of income that is not counted for tax purposes
senses.definitionCN: 在计税时不计入收入的项目
senses.example: The tax exclusion for employer health cover reduced the bill.
senses.exampleCN: 雇主医保的免税待遇降低了税单。
senses.why: The tax base is a defined set. An exclusion removes one item before the rate is applied, so the item never enters the calculation.
senses.whyCN: 税基是一个被定义的集合。exclusion 在套用税率前移走一项，因此该项从未进入计算。

senses.title: Expulsion from an institution
senses.titleCN: 逐出：被学校或组织开除
senses.definition: the removal of a person from a school, club, or organization as a punishment
senses.definitionCN: 作为惩罚把某人从学校、俱乐部或组织中除名
senses.example: The exclusion was reduced to a suspension on appeal.
senses.exampleCN: 经上诉，开除处分被减为停学。
senses.why: An institution controls its own door. Expulsion is exclusion made punitive: the person is not merely outside but formally put outside.
senses.whyCN: 机构控制自己的门。开除是带惩罚性的 exclusion：当事人不仅在门外，而且是被正式放到门外。

senses.title: Exclusivity
senses.titleCN: 排他性：只让一部分人进入的安排
senses.definition: the quality of an arrangement that admits only a limited set of people
senses.definitionCN: 只接纳有限人群的安排所具有的性质
senses.example: The club's exclusion was part of its appeal.
senses.exampleCN: 这家俱乐部的排他性正是其吸引力的一部分。
senses.why: Here exclusion is valued rather than resented: the closed door itself becomes the product, because being inside signals membership.
senses.whyCN: 这里的排斥被珍视而非怨恨：关着的门本身成了产品，因为‘在里面’标志着 membership。

intro.en: Exclusion is from Latin exclusio, from excludere, to shut out: ex- out plus claudere to shut. The same claudere runs through include, conclude, and clause.
intro.cn: exclusion 来自拉丁 exclusio，源头是 excludere‘关在外面’：ex-‘向外’加 claudere‘关’。同一个 claudere 贯穿 include、conclude 与 clause。

items.en: To shut, close, or enclose. It gives English close, clause, cloister, and the -clude verbs. The root image is a door or a barrier.
items.cn: 关、闭、围住。它给出英语 close、clause、cloister 以及 -clude 系列动词。词根意象是门或障碍。

items.en: Ex- out plus claudere shut: to shut out, exclude, or cut off. The verb assumes an inside that is being protected.
items.cn: ex-‘向外’加 claudere‘关’：关在外面、排除、切断。该动词预设了一个被保护的‘里面’。

items.en: A shutting out. In rhetoric it could also mean omission or rejection of a possibility; in law, a bar to entry.
items.cn: 关在外面。在修辞学里也可指省略或排除某种可能；在法律里指禁止进入。

items.en: French passed the noun to English. The legal sense of a bar or an exception travelled with it.
items.cn: 法语把名词传给英语，禁止进入或除外条款的法律义随之而来。

items.en: English exclusion is recorded in the 15c. Early uses were legal and institutional: exclusion from office, from a court, from a will.
items.cn: 英语 exclusion 在 15 世纪有记录。早期用法是法律与制度性的：排除公职、排除法庭、排除继承。

items.en: The 20c added social exclusion and competitive exclusion, extending the closed door from law to society and ecology.
items.cn: 20 世纪加入社会排斥与竞争排斥，把‘关上的门’从法律扩展到社会与生态。

note.en: The first group is the exclude family; the second compares ways of removing someone or something, each with a different mechanism.
note.cn: 第一组是 exclude 词族；第二组比较把人或物移走的不同方式，各自机制不同。

entries.definition: to shut someone or something out. It is the action; exclusion is the act or state.
entries.definitionCN: 把人或物关在外面；是动作，exclusion 是行为或状态。

entries.definition: limited to a particular group, or not shared. It describes the arrangement, not the act of shutting.
entries.definitionCN: 限于特定群体的，或不共享的；描述安排，而非关门动作。

entries.definition: only, and to the exclusion of everything else. It turns the adjective into a restriction on scope.
entries.definitionCN: 只；唯独；把其他一切排除在外。它把形容词变成范围限制。

entries.definition: tending to exclude people or things. It is used of rules, practices, and policies.
entries.definitionCN: 倾向于排斥人或物的；用于规则、做法与政策。

entries.definition: something left out, often by mistake or by choice in writing. It does not require a door or a boundary.
entries.definitionCN: 被漏掉的东西，常因疏忽或书写选择；不需要门或边界。

entries.definition: the act of taking something away from its place. It focuses on the object being moved, not on who is kept out.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物从其位置拿走；聚焦被移动的对象，而不是被挡在外面的人。

entries.definition: the act of forcing someone or something out, often physically. It is more violent than exclusion.
entries.definitionCN: 强行把人或物弄出去，常是物理性的；比 exclusion 更暴力。

entries.definition: the deliberate avoidance or shunning of a person by a group. It is exclusion carried out by many small refusals.
entries.definitionCN: 群体对某人有意回避、排斥；是许多次小拒绝共同完成的 exclusion。

entries.definition: the enforced separation of groups, especially by race or sex. It divides space rather than simply shutting one door.
entries.definitionCN: 按种族或性别等强制分隔群体；它分割空间，而不只是关一扇门。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: ex- out plus claudere shut. Exclusion is the closing of a door in someone's face, seen either as an act or as a state.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：ex-‘向外’加 claudere‘关’。exclusion 就是在某人面前关门，可作为动作也可作为状态来看。

normal.en: Ex- out, claudere shut: exclusion is being shut out.
normal.cn: ex- 向外，claudere 关：exclusion 就是被关在外面。

normal.en: Include and exclude are the two directions of the same door.
normal.cn: include 与 exclude 是同一扇门的两个方向。

normal.en: An exclusion clause is a door drawn on paper.
normal.cn: 除外条款就是画在纸上的一扇门。

normal.en: Social exclusion closes many doors at once.
normal.cn: 社会排斥同时关上许多扇门。

normal.en: A club's exclusion is its selling point: the closed door is the product.
normal.cn: 俱乐部的排他性就是卖点：关着的门本身是产品。

abstract.en: Every inside is made by an outside; exclusion is how a group learns its own shape.
abstract.cn: 每个‘里面’都由‘外面’造出；排斥是群体认识自身形状的方式。

abstract.en: The same closed door can be a punishment or a privilege, depending on which side you stand.
abstract.cn: 同一扇关着的门，可以是惩罚也可以是特权，取决于你站在哪一侧。

abstract.en: Exclusion is cheaper than inclusion, which is why systems drift toward it.
abstract.cn: 排斥比容纳便宜，所以系统会自然漂向排斥。

examples.en: The exclusion of the small firms from the scheme was challenged in court.
examples.cn: 把小公司排除在该计划之外的做法在法庭上受到挑战。

examples.en: He worked on the project to the exclusion of almost everything else.
examples.cn: 他做这个项目，几乎把其他一切排除在外。

examples.en: The report treated social exclusion as a health issue, not only a moral one.
examples.cn: 报告把社会排斥当作健康问题，而不只是道德问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: “一颗死路”——走到一颗标着‘死路’的门前，被关在外面：exclusion 排除、排斥。

root: 源自拉丁 excludere（ex-‘向外’+ claudere‘关’）与 exclusio‘关在外面’；核心是“把某人或某物挡在门外的动作或状态”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of exclusion, one image: a door closes and someone stays outside. The door may be a club, a contract, a society, a niche, a tax base, a school, or a membership rule.
sensesIntro.cn: exclusion 的八个义项共用一个意象：门关上，有人留在外面。这扇门可以是俱乐部、合同、社会、生态位、税基、学校或会员规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door closing with a person left in the corridor.
core.cn: 核心意象：门关上，一个人被留在走廊里。

branches.en: THE TWO SIDES OF THE DOOR: the act of shutting out and the experience of being outside.
branches.cn: 门的两侧：关门的动作与留在外面的经历。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN BOUNDARY: insurance clauses and tax rules remove items before they count.
branches.cn: 写下的边界：保险条款与税务规则在计算前移走项目。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL AND PUNITIVE DOOR: structural marginalization and formal expulsion both put a person outside.
branches.cn: 社会性与惩罚性的门：结构性边缘化与正式开除都把一个人放到外面。

branches.en: THE ECOLOGICAL DOOR: competition closes a niche on a rival species.
branches.cn: 生态的门：竞争对竞争者关上生态位。

branches.en: THE VALUED DOOR: exclusivity makes the closed door itself desirable.
branches.cn: 被珍视的门：排他性让关着的门本身变得有吸引力。

intro.en: Exclusion is ex- plus claud- plus -sion. The same root gives include, conclude, seclude, and the noun clause; the door image is shared across all of them.
intro.cn: exclusion 是 ex- 加 claud- 加 -sion。同一词根给出 include、conclude、seclude 与名词 clause；它们共享‘门’的意象。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms are claudere, excludere, and exclusio. Excludere is built from a real prefix and a real verb, so no reconstruction is needed here.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁形式是 claudere、excludere、exclusio。excludere 由真实前缀与真实动词构成，这里不需要重构。

items.meaning: to shut out or leave out
items.exampleCN: 规则排除迟交的参赛作品。

items.meaning: the act or state of being shut out
items.example: His exclusion from the team was temporary.
items.exampleCN: 他被排除在队伍之外是暂时的。

items.meaning: restricted to a few; not shared

items.example: The room is used exclusively for meetings.

items.meaning: the state of being restricted to a few
items.exampleCN: 这个品牌为排他性收费。

items.example: The zoning rules had an exclusionary effect.
items.exampleCN: 分区规则产生了排斥效果。

items.meaning: to shut inside, hence to contain
items.meaningCN: 包含；把……关在里面（in-‘在内’+ claudere‘关’）

items.meaning: to close together, hence to end or infer
items.meaningCN: 结束；得出结论（com-‘一起’+ claudere‘关’）
items.example: The talk concluded with a short summary.

items.meaning: to shut apart, hence to isolate
items.meaningCN: 使隔离；隐居（se-‘分开’+ claudere‘关’）
items.example: The cabin was secluded by tall pines.
items.exampleCN: 小屋被高松林隔离起来。

items.meaning: a distinct part of a sentence or contract
items.meaningCN: 从句；条款；源自‘关闭、收束的部分’
items.example: The final clause limits the agreement to five years.
items.exampleCN: 最后一条条款把协议限制在五年内。
